title: km-ast: domain model for knowledge tree
description:
Design the km-ast domain model: a clean, type-based node hierarchy replacing the current 14-type flat enum with extractBody heuristic.

Core changes:
- Two node kinds: Item (oi, li) and Block (p, h, code, quote, table, hr, html, embed)
- OutlineItem (oi) + fstype replaces folder/file/section
- ListItem (li) replaces ul/ol/task — marker field preserves style
- Task is a trait (task_status), not a type
- Items have .blocks[] and .subitems[] (uniform split rule)
- li has .blocks[] (same as oi), no separate .content
- "h" (heading) and "embed" are block types
- Heading level implicit from tree depth
- 14 types → 10 types
- Eliminates extractBody and 12+ duplicate call sites

Deliverables:
1. Finalized type definitions (km-ast)
2. Test fixtures: markdown → AST transformation examples
3. Migration plan from current types
design:
## km-ast: Domain Model for Knowledge Tree

### Core Principle

Two independent hierarchies sharing one physical table, with type determining role.

### Terminology

- **title**: computed display text for navigation/outline. Resolution: blocks[0].content → name → id
- **heading**: a block type (h) representing a markdown heading (## text). Styled prominently in doc view.
- **name**: stored identity string (filename, slug). May or may not match title.
- **marker**: prefix decoration on a line item. Both list style and task checkbox are "markers."

### Node Hierarchy

```
NodeBase { id, parent_id, parent_idx, data, created_at, updated_at, version }

Block extends NodeBase {
  type: BlockType       // p | h | code | quote | table | hr | html
  content: string       // markdown text (inline formatting preserved as string)
}

ItemBase extends NodeBase {
  .blocks[]    — derived: children where type is not own type
  .subitems[]  — derived: children where type matches own type
  // blocks[0] = title/heading when present
  // blocks always sort before subitems in parent_idx
  // NO content field — display text comes from blocks[0].content
}

OutlineItem extends ItemBase {
  type: "oi"
  fstype: repo | folder | file | mdfile | mdsection
  name?: string             — filesystem identity / heading slug
  task_marker?: string      — "[x]", "[ ]", "[/]", "[!]", "[-]"
}

ListItem extends ItemBase {
  type: "li"
  list_marker: string       — "-", "*", "+", "1.", "1)", "[^1]", "[^note]"
  task_marker?: string      — "[x]", "[ ]", "[/]", "[!]", "[-]" (optional)
}

Link extends NodeBase {
  type: "link"
  link_to: string           — target node ID
  embed: boolean            — true = transclude, false = reference
  .blocks[]                 — optional: alias/override content (blocks[0] = alias)
}

type BlockType = "p" | "h" | "code" | "quote" | "table" | "hr" | "html"  // 7
type ItemType = "oi" | "li"                                                // 2
type LinkType = "link"                                                     // 1
type NodeType = BlockType | ItemType | LinkType                            // 10

type Item = OutlineItem | ListItem
type Node = Block | Item | Link
```

### Three Categories

1. **Blocks** (7 types): content leaves with a content string
2. **Items** (2 types): structural nodes with .blocks[] and .subitems[]
3. **Links** (1 type): references to other nodes, optionally with alias blocks

### Two Independent Hierarchies

- **Outline tree** (sectioning): oi → oi → oi (repo, folders, files, sections)
- **List trees** (flow): li → li → li (rooted inside outline item body)
- **Inline** (phrasing): bold, links, code (within content string, NOT nodes)

### Children Split (uniform rule)

```typescript
// Same rule for both oi and li:
item.subitems = children.filter(c => c.type === item.type)
item.blocks   = children.filter(c => c.type !== item.type)
// Link nodes fall into .blocks[] — they're body content
```

### Ordering

Blocks always sort before subitems in parent_idx. No interleaving.

### Title Resolution

Every item resolves to a display title:
  blocks[0].content → name → id

- blocks[0]: first block's content (h, p, or link's alias)
- name: filesystem identity / heading slug
- id: the node's ULID (last resort, shown distinctly in UI)

Heading level: implicit from tree depth (never stored).

| fstype     | name source       | blocks[0]              | Sync               |
|------------|-------------------|------------------------|---------------------|
| repo       | repo name         | from index .md if any  | name → display      |
| folder     | dirname           | from index .md if any  | name → display      |
| file/mdfile| filename sans .md | H1 content (required)  | name ↔ title        |
| mdsection  | slugified heading | heading text           | title → name        |

File rule: one and only one H1 required for file/mdfile (blocks[0] of type "h").
Folders: optional index file (folder.md, README.md, .md) provides body/metadata.

### Task Trait

Any Item can be a task via task_marker. task_status is derived:

| task_marker | Status    |
|-------------|-----------|
| "[ ]"       | todo      |
| "[x]"/"[X]" | done     |
| "[/]"       | wip       |
| "[!]"       | blocked   |
| "[-]"       | dropped   |
| absent      | not a task|

### List Markers

Unordered: "-", "*", "+"
Ordered: "1.", "1)", "3." (start number + delimiter)
Footnote: "[^1]", "[^note]"

Footnote definitions ([^1]: text) are li nodes with footnote-style list_marker.
References ([^1]) stay inline in content strings.

### Links

type: "link" with embed flag:
- ![[target]] → link(embed:true) — transclude target content
- [[target]] as standalone → link(embed:false) — reference card
- [[target]] inline in text → stays in content string, indexed in links table
- Alias: ![[target|alias]] → link with p(content:"alias") as blocks[0]

### Skipped Heading Levels

H1 → H3 (skipping H2) inserts synthetic oi at missing level.
Round-trip normalizes (serializes as H1 → H2 → H3). No hints stored.

### Type Enum (10 values)

```typescript
type BlockType = "p" | "h" | "code" | "quote" | "table" | "hr" | "html"  // 7
type ItemType = "oi" | "li"                                                // 2
type LinkType = "link"                                                     // 1
type NodeType = BlockType | ItemType | LinkType                            // 10
```

### Predicates

```typescript
const isOutline  = (t: NodeType) => t === "oi"
const isListItem = (t: NodeType) => t === "li"
const isItem     = (t: NodeType) => t === "oi" || t === "li"
const isLink     = (t: NodeType) => t === "link"
const isBlock    = (t: NodeType) => !isItem(t) && !isLink(t)
```

isOutline replaces: extractBody, NON_COLUMN_TYPES, BODY_TYPES, STRUCTURAL_TYPES — all 12+ call sites.

### Changes from Current (14 → 10 types)

- folder/file/section → oi + fstype
- paragraph → p
- ul/ol/task → li + list_marker + task_marker
- embed → link (type, with embed flag)
- NEW: h (heading block)
- code, quote, table, hr, html → unchanged
- agent, board → removed (data-layer concern)
notes:
Deep research review (O3, 2026-02-13): Model validated against mdast, Notion, ProseMirror, Slate, Org-mode, BlockSuite/Logseq/Roam. Top findings:

1. COMPLETENESS: 10 types cover major blocks. Gaps: frontmatter (handled via data field on file oi), images (inline in content), math blocks (future: code with lang=math), admonitions (future: quote with marker). All acceptable.

2. PRIOR ART: Model is closest to Notion's block model + Org-mode's outline structure. Both validate the approach. Flattened lists (no container nodes) match Notion. Heading-as-container matches Org-mode.

3. LINK TYPE: Confirmed as lightweight pointer — all prior art (Obsidian, Logseq, Roam) treats embeds as references, never duplicating subtree. Keep as third category, not Item.

4. MARKERS: O3 recommends boolean checked + minimal markers. We chose literal strings (task_marker='[x]', list_marker='-') for round-trip fidelity. This is a deliberate trade-off documented in model.md.

5. FOOTNOTES AS LI: 'Unconventional but workable.' GFM spec itself says footnote defs work like multi-paragraph list items. [^ marker pattern is unique enough. Acceptable.

6. HEADING NORMALIZATION: No other tool auto-corrects. Our choice is opinionated but workable for an integrated tool. Documented.

7. MIGRATION GOTCHAS: (a) Insert h child nodes for each section title, (b) combine ul/ol/task into li with markers, (c) handle agent/board removal, (d) enforce blocks-before-subitems ordering.

Docs updated: model.md (added content model, frontmatter, inline content, design decisions), concepts.md, storage.md, ref/markdown.md (all cross-referenced).

description: Breadcrumb shows 'ainbox' instead of 'inbox', 'CTaskNotes' instead of 'TaskNotes'. First char of previous nav target leaks into current breadcrumb. Confirmed at 120x40 and 80x24. Screenshot: /tmp/explore-screenshots/14-navigate-right.png
notes:
REPRODUCER RESULT: NOT reproducible in TUI tests or VirtualTerminal ANSI replay. Tried simple and complex fixtures (varying name lengths, rapid h/l/h/l). Buffer is correct, ANSI replay is correct. Likely a real-terminal-only rendering issue. Tests: tmp-explore-tests/breadcrumb-ghost.test.ts, breadcrumb-ghost-v2.test.ts
Fix applied: Changed top bar Box from default flexDirection (row) to flexDirection='column'. In row layout, the Text child's width was its intrinsic content width. When navigating and the breadcrumb text got shorter, the Text's layout shrank, but the parent Box's bg fill was skipped (contentAreaAffected=false for the Box since only a child changed). This meant stale characters from the previous longer text remained in the terminal buffer at positions beyond the new text's layout. With flexDirection='column', the Text stretches to the full parent width (cross-axis stretching), so its layout always covers termWidth regardless of content length. clearNodeRegion then covers the full width. Test: apps/km-tui/tests/breadcrumb-ghost.test.ts (3 tests). Layer 1 done.
Session 0218b: FIXED in inkx vendor. renderText() now clears trailing cells after shorter text. renderTextLineReturn/renderAnsiTextLineReturn return end column for cleanup. 119 inkx test files (2110 tests) pass. 3 breadcrumb tests pass. Needs user verification.

**Challenge**: A card contains a tree of nodes (title, body lines, child nodes). Each may have its own TextInput/TextArea. The click needs to: (1) identify which text region was clicked, (2) position the cursor within that region, (3) if clicked between regions (e.g., on indent/bullet), snap to the nearest text boundary.

title: Card content lines wrap instead of truncating at line end
description:
Reported many times. In cards view, child content lines (list items, paragraphs) inside cards wrap to multiple lines instead of being truncated with ellipsis at the line boundary.

Screenshot shows paths like 'Accessible at /Library/Mobile Documents/comapple~CloudDocs/' wrapping to 2 lines, and 'Early Orbit/ — Business, product/engineering docs (.numbers, .key, .p…' wrapping to 3 lines.

Root cause: In cards view, child TreeNodes (depth > 0) render in multiline mode with no height constraint and no overflow='hidden'. Their content text wraps freely. Each child line should be height={1} with wrap='truncate'.

Fix location: TreeNode.tsx — when rendering children inside a card (multiline variant, depth > 0), each child's content should be single-line truncated.

title: Card title word-wrap breaks mid-expression
description: Card title wraps incorrectly: 'US$ 3k x 4 = $12k + $400-700/mo' breaks after '$12k' leaving '+' orphaned on next line. The wrap should keep the + with adjacent content.
notes: Fix: Added isBreakBeforeOperator() look-ahead in wrapText(). When a space precedes a single non-alphanumeric character followed by another space (infix operator pattern like ' + ', ' = ', ' | '), the space is not recorded as a word boundary break point. This prevents operators from being orphaned at the start of wrapped lines. Files: vendor/beorn-inkx/src/unicode.ts, vendor/beorn-inkx/tests/unicode.test.ts. All 325 unicode tests pass + 2184 vendor tests pass.

title: Card memo: use reference equality with structural sharing instead of field-by-field comparison
description:
Currently CardColumn.tsx has a growing field-by-field React.memo comparison (id, content, task_status, due_date, priority, recurrence, etc.) that must be updated every time a new KNode display field is added. Two misaligned memo comparisons exist: Card memo in CardColumn.tsx and TreeNode memo in TreeNode.tsx.

Better approach: align object reference changes with caching/memoization. Options:
1. Single 'card' reference that changes when any display-relevant field changes (structural sharing in useColumns/deriveColumnsFromRepo)
2. Split card into sub-objects (card.body, card.title, card.meta) where each reference changes independently — more granular re-renders
3. Just compare card.node by reference, with node interning in the repo layer

The key insight: instead of duplicating field lists in memo comparisons, make the object references themselves be the memoization signal. This eliminates the class of bugs where a new field (like due_date) is added to KNode but forgotten in the memo comparison.

title: Chord second key leaks into dialog text input
description:
When pressing a chord like 'td' (set due date), the second key 'd' (and sometimes preceding navigation keys) leak into the dialog's text input field.

Reproduction:
1. Navigate to a task card
2. Press 'td' chord to open date dialog
3. Observe: input field contains 'd' (or other leaked chars like 'rnjtd')

Expected: Input field should be empty when dialog opens.

Root cause hypothesis: The chord system processes 't' (starts chord timer), then 'd' completes the chord and opens the dialog. But the 'd' keystroke also gets processed as a text input event because the dialog's useEditContext registers its input handler asynchronously — the 'd' arrives before the dialog's input layer is on top of the stack.

Related: This is an input layer timing issue. The chord handler opens the dialog, but the same keystroke event continues propagating to the newly-mounted dialog's text input.

title: Mouse click targeting unreliable — use DOM hit testing instead of Y-offset math
description: resolveMouseTarget() in board-app.ts uses manual Y-offset math to determine which block was clicked inside a card. This is unreliable because: (1) blockIndex is clamped to children.length (direct children only), so nested visible descendants map to the wrong node, (2) the Y-offset calculation assumes each child = 1 row, which breaks with variable-height content. inkx already has DOM-style hitTest() that walks the render tree and finds the deepest element at (x,y) using screenRect — just like web browsers. The fix: use hitTest to find the clicked element, then walk up to find the nearest node with an id prop. This replaces all manual coordinate math with reliable tree-based hit testing.

title: Precise click targeting: columns, card titles, sub-blocks
description:
Click interactions should be more precise and work at all levels:

## Column-level clicks
- Clicking a column header selects that column (moves cursor to it)
- Clicking empty space in a column selects the column

## Card-level clicks  
- Clicking the card title/heading = select the card (move cursor to it)
- Single click on a sub-item/block within a card = select that specific block
- Double-click on a sub-item = edit that block inline

## Current behavior
- Click resolves to a card via resolveMouseToNode() using GridNavigator position registry
- Double-click enters inline edit on the whole card
- No column-level click handling
- No sub-block precision

## Implementation notes
- resolveMouseToNode() in board-app.ts does column→card resolution
- Need to extend to resolve card→block (sub-item level)
- GridNavigator tracks card positions but not sub-item positions
- May need to register sub-item positions or use relative Y offset within card

comments.author: claude:97b8de73
comments.text:
Phase 2 Research: Sub-block precision

Current state:
- resolveMouseTarget() already computes blockIndex from relative Y within card
- Click handler navigates to child nodes using getVisibleDescendantIds()
- Sub-block targeting works via fixed 1-row-per-child assumption

What would improve it:
- Register child positions in navigator for pixel-perfect hit testing
- Current 1-row-per-child breaks for wrapped titles or variable-height children
- TreeNode would need useScreenRectCallback for each child
- Perf concern: N children * M cards * K columns = many registrations
- Alternative: use card bounding box + relative Y (current approach) but account for variable row heights by reading actual rendered content dimensions

notes: User insight: subIndex is a code smell. Everything is a tree — the cursor should be a node ID (already cursorCardNodeId exists). Selecting a subitem = cursor points to a child node, not a separate numeric index. This is part of the broader 'cursor is a tree path' direction. Quick fix: only render subIndex highlight on cursor card. Proper fix: replace subIndex with cursorNodeId pointing to the child node directly.

2026-02-24: Deep investigation of garbled rendering / grey line / column header dup

Three output-level fixes applied:
1. fix(output): reset SGR before EL to prevent background color margin bleed (25a121f)
   - bufferToAnsi() emitted \x1b[K] while bg was active → right margin filled with color

   - Forces bufferToAnsi on every frame, bypassing changesToAnsi
   - If garbling disappears with this → bug is in incremental diff serialization

3. feat(output): INKX_STRICT_OUTPUT=1 verification (690f141)
   - Replays changesToAnsi output through virtual terminal
   - Compares resulting screen to fresh render
   - Catches output-level bugs that buffer-level INKX_STRICT cannot detect

Investigation results:
- INKX_STRICT (buffer-level): PASSES — buffers are correct
- INKX_STRICT_OUTPUT (ANSI-level): PASSES — character positions are correct
- This means the garbling is NOT character misplacement
- Remaining hypothesis: style/color state issue or Ghostty-specific rendering

Diagnostic commands for user testing:
  INKX_FULL_RENDER=1 bun km:strict view --repo imports/asana stabell
  INKX_STRICT_OUTPUT=1 bun km:strict view --repo imports/asana stabell
2026-02-24 12:25: User reports garbled rendering persists after DEC 2026 sync disable.
Screenshot: ~/Desktop/Screenshot 2026-02-24 at 12.25.32.png
Visible issues: duplicate column headers (beowa/beowa, bjørn/bjørn), truncated top bar.
This confirms the col-header-dup bug is SEPARATE from the Ghostty DEC 2026 sync issue.
The sync bug caused progressive corruption; this is a style transition bug in changesToAnsi
where background color changes (undefined→yellow) aren't being emitted as cell updates.
All verification layers pass because they check characters, not SGR styles.
2026-02-24: ROOT CAUSE FOUND — dirty row desync in runtime's diff layer

The production path (createApp) has TWO ANSI output mechanisms:
1. Pipeline: executeRender() → outputPhase() produces ANSI (DISCARDED in createApp!)
2. Runtime: runtime.render() → diff() → outputPhase() produces ANSI (actually written to stdout)

When processEventBatch triggers multiple doRender() calls (layout feedback, effects):
- Each doRender advances _prevTermBuffer (pipeline's chain)
- But runtime.render() is called ONCE at the end
- runtime.prevBuffer is still from the PREVIOUS event batch

The final buffer's dirty rows only cover the LAST doRender's changes. But diffBuffers()
uses dirty rows to narrow its scan. Rows changed in earlier doRenders but not the last
one are invisible → skipped → garbled terminal output.

Fix: markAllRowsDirty() on the final buffer when flushCount > 0 (multiple doRenders).
This forces diffBuffers to do a full scan, finding all changes relative to runtime's
older prevBuffer.

Files changed:
- vendor/beorn-inkx/src/buffer.ts: Added markAllRowsDirty() method
- vendor/beorn-inkx/src/runtime/create-app.tsx: Call markAllRowsDirty() after flush loop
2026-02-24 14:10 — CRITICAL DISCOVERY: INKX_STRICT verification gap. processEventBatch resets _renderCount=0, doRender increments to 1, check requires >1. Navigation renders were NEVER verified. This explains why 'INKX_STRICT passes' during navigation — it wasn't running. Fixed: replaced _renderCount>1 with wasIncremental flag (create-app.tsx). User must re-test with INKX_STRICT=1 to see if content-phase bugs are now caught during navigation. See km-silvery-legacy.strict-rendercount.
2026-02-24 14:30 — ROOT CAUSE FOUND: Commit 6e35fe2 (perf: strip Box/Text overhead + fix content-phase skip) replaced the layoutChanged catch-all (always true due to stale prevLayout=null) with layoutChangedThisFrame flag. This exposed latent dirty flag propagation bugs — nodes that should be re-rendered are being skipped because they have no dirty flags. INKX_STRICT now catches these (after _renderCount fix). FIX: Reverted layoutChanged back to !rectEqual(prevLayout,contentRect) without syncPrevLayout — restores the catch-all. O(N) content phase but correct. Created km-silvery-legacy.content-phase-skip for the proper optimization.

title: Column headers truncated: missing last character (SCHEDUL, PORTFOLI)

notes:
Root cause: PUA character width mismatch. Nerdfont icons (U+E000-U+F8FF) reported as 1-cell by string-width but rendered as 2-cell by modern terminals (Ghostty, Kitty, iTerm2). This 1-column mismatch shifts all text after the icon right by 1, clipping the last character at the column boundary. No ellipsis shown because inkx truncation logic (using same width calc) thinks text fits.

Fix: add re-entrancy guard to store subscription (skip doRender if already rendering), or batch set() calls, or use queueMicrotask to defer re-render. title: Delete key: forward delete with merge-with-next at boundary
description:
Implement Delete key (forward delete) as the mirror of Backspace, with smart boundary behavior.

## Text Edit Mode

### Mid-content
Already works: deleteForward() removes char after cursor.

### At end of content (cursor at content.length)
Merge next sibling into current node:
- Current node survives (keeps type, traits, depth)
- Next sibling's text is appended to current content
- Next sibling is deleted

Edge cases (mirror of mergeWithPrevious):
- Next exists, empty, no children → delete next
- Next exists, has content, no children → append next text to current, delete next
- Next exists, has children → append text, reparent children under current
- No next sibling → boundary (bell)

### On empty node
Delete on empty = delete the node (same as backspace-on-empty). Symmetric behavior.

## Node Mode (not editing)
Delete key in node mode = noop. Only D (capital) deletes nodes with confirmation. Delete key is too easy to hit accidentally.

## Implementation

1. Add mergeWithNext() to km-tree/block-ops.ts (mirror of mergeWithPrevious)
2. Update TEXT_DELETE_FORWARD in board-actions.ts with smart boundary check
3. Tests for mergeWithNext + integration tests for the full flow

title: Detail pane: right border segments render black instead of border color
notes:
## Root Cause Analysis

The `renderBorder()` function in `vendor/beorn-inkx/src/pipeline/render-box.ts` was setting border cells with only `char` and `fg`, leaving `bg` to default to `null` (transparent/terminal-default). However, the Box's background fill (which runs just before border rendering) sets all cells including border positions to `bg=0` (explicit black for backgroundColor="black"). The border `setCell` then overwrites `bg` to `null`, creating a discrepancy:

- Content cells inside the box: `bg=0` (explicit black, emits \x1b[48;5;0m)
- Border cells: `bg=null` (no bg SGR emitted, terminal uses default)

In terminals where palette color 0 (black) differs from the default background, or where ANSI handling of transitions between explicit and default backgrounds has subtle rendering differences, this causes border segments to appear visually different from the surrounding box.

## Fix

Modified `renderBorder()` to pass `bg` from `props.backgroundColor` (parsed via `parseColor()`) to all border cell `setCell` calls. Border cells now have the same bg as the rest of the box:
- Box with backgroundColor="black": border cells get bg=0
- Box with backgroundColor="cyan": border cells get bg=6
- Box without backgroundColor: border cells get bg=null (unchanged behavior)

## Files Changed

- `vendor/beorn-inkx/src/pipeline/render-box.ts` — `renderBorder()` now sets `bg` from box backgroundColor
- `vendor/beorn-inkx/tests/detail-pane-border.test.tsx` — New test file verifying border cell fg and bg consistency

## Test Results

- All 2115 inkx tests pass (120 files)

title: Detail pane: group date fields together after Status
Detail pane: column-like focus, navigation, and selection highlighting
description:
## Problem

The detail pane doesn't behave like a proper focusable pane. When you move focus to it, there's no clear visual feedback about what's selected, navigation (j/k) doesn't work intuitively through the content sections, and properties aren't individually focusable. The unfocused pane also doesn't dim its selection state.

## Design: Column-Like Detail Pane

The detail pane should render **like a board column** — with the same focus/selection visual language:

### 1. Top Bar = Column Header

The top bar (currently via PaneBar) should behave like a column header:
- **When detail pane is focused**: top bar background = `$selected` (gold), text = `$selectedfg` (black) — just like a selected column header
- **When detail pane is NOT focused**: top bar uses current unfocused style (`$muted` bg, dimmed text)
- The "selected item" in the detail pane is the item itself by default (the top bar)

### 2. j/k Navigation Through Sections

When the detail pane is focused, j/k should move a cursor through focusable sections:
- **Top bar** (the item itself) — default selection
- **Each metadata property** (status, priority, due date, assigned, projects, tags, etc.)
- **Body content** (as a single block or per-block)
- **Subitems** (each subitem individually)
- **Backlinks** (each backlink individually)

This is the existing `detailCursorNodeId` system but extended to cover ALL sections, not just folder outline entries and backlinks.

### 3. Focusable Properties

Metadata properties should be individually selectable. When cursored:
- Highlighted with `$selected`/`$selectedfg` (same as a selected card)
- Enter could open an edit dialog for that property
- This enables keyboard-driven metadata editing

### 4. Dimming the Unfocused Pane

Whichever pane is NOT focused should dim its `$selected`/`$selectedbg`:
- **Board unfocused**: Already partially implemented — `borderDimColor={!boardFocused}` on cards
- **Detail pane unfocused**: Selection highlight should dim (use `dimColor` on the top bar and any cursored items)
- The key visual: you always know which pane is active by which one has bright gold vs dim gold

## Current State

- `DetailPane.tsx`: Has `isFocused` prop but uses it minimally
- `PaneBar.tsx`: Focused = `$border` bg, unfocused = `$muted` bg + dimColor — but NOT `$selected` (gold) like column headers
- `detailCursorNodeId`: Exists in store but only navigates folder outline (depth=0) and backlinks
- `CardColumn.tsx`: Has good selection/dimming patterns to replicate
- `board-pills.ts` `getHeaderStyle()`: Column header gold styling — detail pane should use the same pattern

## Implementation Approach

1. **Extend cursor model**: `detailCursorNodeId` → support section-based cursor (top-bar, meta:status, meta:priority, ..., body, subitem:id, backlink:id)
2. **PaneBar for detail**: When focused + cursor on top bar → gold background (like column header)
3. **Metadata rows**: Each row gets a focusable identity, cursor highlights with `$selected`
4. **Dim unfocused**: Both panes apply `dimColor` to their selection indicators when not focused
5. **Navigation commands**: Register j/k handlers for detail pane context (when detail focused)
notes:
## Implementation (2026-02-28)

### Done
1. **Topbar cursor**: `DETAIL_TOPBAR_ID` ("__topbar__") — cursor defaults here when entering detail pane via `l`
2. **Metadata row navigation**: `DETAIL_META_PREFIX` ("__meta__") + key (e.g., "__meta__Status") — j/k moves through metadata rows
3. **Gold top bar**: When focused + cursor on topbar, PaneBar uses `$selected` bg + `$selectedfg` text (like selected column headers)
4. **Metadata row highlight**: Cursored metadata rows use `inverse` styling
5. **Board dimming**: Already works — `boardFocused` controls dimColor on cards/columns when detail pane is focused
6. **Tests**: 5 new tests in detail-pane.test.ts covering topbar cursor, j/k nav, metadata, folder detail

### Commits
- e5aa2494 feat(tui): detail pane topbar cursor + item improvements
- d685bd5c feat(tui): detail pane column-like focus with topbar cursor and metadata navigation

### Remaining
- Verify visually (TTY/user confirmation needed)
- Detail pane selection dimming when unfocused (detail cursor indicator should dim when board is focused)

### Architecture notes:

- Navigable item list is computed in detail-pane-items.ts (getDetailItemsForNode)
- Keybindings are in keybindings.ts layer 6 (detail-pane group)

### Visual fixes DONE (this session):

2. Added DetailPaneTopBar with icon + title via PaneBar
3. Removed duplicate title, 'Contents:', separator from body
4. WorkspaceView wraps detail panes in PaneLabelProvider
5. Tests updated and passing (59/59)

4. Body blocks (paragraphs/code) navigable

Visual fixes (bg, top bar, duplicate removal) complete.

title: Detail pane content lags 2-3s behind title on cursor change
description:
When cursor changes on main board, the detail pane title updates immediately but content stays stale for 2-3s before catching up.

**Expected**: Either content updates immediately with the title, or a loading indicator is shown until content is in sync with the pane title.

**Current**: Title changes instantly, stale content from previous node remains visible for 2-3s, then new content appears. This creates a confusing mismatch where the title says one thing and the content shows another.

**Likely cause**: Detail pane title reads from cursor state directly (synchronous), but content reads from a derived/async source (repo query, markdown parse, or debounced update). The fix should either make content synchronous or add a loading state when title !== content's source node.
notes:
## Root Cause

The `useColumns` hook in `apps/km-tui/src/hooks/use-columns.ts` used a `useState` + `useEffect` pattern for column derivation. When `rootId` changes (detail pane following cursor), the title updates synchronously (from Jotai nodeStore atoms in BoardTopBar), but column content was deferred to post-render via useEffect, creating 1+ frames where the title showed the new node but content showed stale columns from the previous node.

## Fix

Added synchronous column derivation during render when rootId changes. React handles setState-during-render by immediately re-rendering with the new state without committing the intermediate frame. The useEffect is kept for version-driven re-derivation (repo mutations) where coalescing is desirable.

## Key code change (use-columns.ts lines 207-218):
```typescript
if (depsRef.current.rootId !== rootId) {
  repo.preloadSubtree(rootId, 3)
  const newColumns = derive(repo, rootId, foldDepthsRef.current)
  depsRef.current = { rootId, version: effectiveVersion }
  setColumns(newColumns)
}
```

## Test Results
- 78/78 detail pane tests pass
- 82/82 fast TUI tests pass
- 37/37 zoom tests pass (+ 1 pre-existing failure in real vault test unrelated to this change)
- 16/16 scroll + fold tests pass
- bun fix blocked by pre-existing oxlint plugin config issue

- Rich text formatting in description (bullet points, links, indentation)
- Subtasks rendered as actual subtask cards with status/assignee/due (Asana shows a subtask list with checkboxes, assignees, due dates)
- Section headers within subtask list (e.g., 'Maybe someday')

**Styling issues:**
- Description text is plain — no bullet points, no bold/italic, no links
- Body content runs together instead of structured paragraphs

**Architecture question: unify node view types.**
Currently we have multiple ways to render a node:
1. Card view (TreeNode.tsx) — compact card in board column
2. Detail pane (DetailPane.tsx) — side panel with metadata + content
3. Zoomed column view — when you Enter into a section
4. Folder detail pane — outline of folder contents

Could the detail pane reuse the same rendering pipeline as cards (TreeNode/ColumnItems) for the content area? This would ensure consistency and reduce code duplication. The detail pane would be: metadata header + card-style content rendering.

See Asana screenshots at ~/Desktop/Screenshot 2026-02-18 at 13.30.49.png and 13.30.55.png for reference.

title: DotzReporter flickers when view exceeds screen height
description:
## Problem
When the DotzReporter output grows taller than the terminal screen height, there's visible flickering during live updates.

## Expected Behavior
Content should scroll smoothly when it exceeds screen height, with the live-updating portion remaining stable.

## Current Behavior
Flickering occurs, possibly due to cursor movement calculations or frame redraw timing.

## Technical Context
- Reporter uses cursor movement (CSI.moveUp) to redraw in place
- Cursor movement is capped to terminal rows to prevent going past screen top
- Content is allowed to scroll naturally when exceeding screen height
- Issue may be in writeFrame() method in infra/vitest-dotz/index.tsx

```bash
bun run test:fast2  # with many packages that trigger file breakout
```

comments.author: claude:8f007ba9
comments.text: Root cause: evaluateAddRule and getEmbedTargetsOnBoard only checked type='link' embed nodes when deduplicating. Markdown-parsed embeds are stored as 'oi' nodes with link_to set, so they were invisible to the dedup checks. Fix: (1) broadened getEmbedTargetsOnBoard SQL to match any node with link_to IS NOT NULL, (2) broadened within-section existingEmbeds check to include any node with link_to, (3) added dedup in nodes2md serializeChildren to skip duplicate embed targets during serialization. Test added to db-rules.test.ts confirming the fix.

title: EditContext: unified text editing primitives in inkx
description:
Create a unified text editing system in inkx based on the W3C EditContext pattern. Factory function (createTermEditContext), not a class — per principles.md.

## What

1. **EditContextLike interface** — W3C-aligned subset: text, selectionStart, selectionEnd, updateText(), updateSelection(), events (textupdate, selectionchange) + term extensions (moveCursor, atBoundary, wrapWidth, stickyX)
2. **createTermEditContext()** factory — uses text-cursor.ts for visual line math, returns plain object implementing EditContextLike
3. **TextOp type** with invertOp() — {type:'insert', offset, text} ↔ {type:'delete', offset, text}. Foundation for ops-based undo.
4. **useEditContext() hook** — React hook wrapping createTermEditContext, manages lifecycle

## Where

All in vendor/beorn-inkx/ (alongside text-cursor.ts). Extract to beorn-editx later (Phase B of docs/future/universal-editor.md).

## Design Constraints (from principles.md)

- Factory function returning plain object, not class
- Explicit DI: createTermEditContext({ text, wrapWidth, ... })
- Symbol.dispose for cleanup
- No globals, no singletons
- Fail loud on invariant violations
- 50+ tests covering EditContext methods + events + text operations

## Replaces

- BlockEditTarget interface (ad-hoc version of EditContext)
- useSlateEdit internal Slate dependency (for text ops)
- useLineEdit separate implementation
- TextArea's independent cursor management

## References

- docs/future/universal-editor.md — Layer 3 (Edit Context)
- W3C EditContext API
- Current: apps/km-tui/src/block-edit-target.ts (BlockEditTarget interface)
- Current: vendor/beorn-inkx/src/text-cursor.ts (Layer 0, stays)
notes:
2026-02-17: MVP-1 implementation complete. 6 files created, 149 tests passing:

Files:
- vendor/beorn-inkx/src/text-ops.ts — TextOp type, applyTextOp, invertTextOp, mergeTextOps (33 tests)
- vendor/beorn-inkx/src/edit-context.ts — EditContextLike interface, createTermEditContext() factory (84 tests)  
- vendor/beorn-inkx/src/hooks/use-edit-context.ts — useEditContext hook, activeEditContextRef, EditTarget (32 tests)
- vendor/beorn-inkx/tests/text-ops.test.ts
- vendor/beorn-inkx/tests/edit-context.test.ts
- vendor/beorn-inkx/tests/use-edit-context.test.tsx
- vendor/beorn-inkx/src/index.ts updated with exports

All 149 tests pass. No existing tests broken. Lint clean on new files.

Next: km-tui.edit-migrate — replace useSlateEdit/useLineEdit/blockEditTargetRef with EditContext.

title: Text typed during inline edit doesn't display (but saves on Enter)
description:
User reports: when editing a body block, typing shows nothing on screen. But pressing Enter saves the typed text AND creates a new node. The Slate editor captures input but InlineEditField doesn't visually update.

Reproduced in TTY emulator: entered edit mode on body block, typed "x" and "y" — neither appeared. Pressed Escape — text showed "vault.fffxy" confirming characters were captured by Slate but never displayed.

Root cause investigation (incomplete):
- Production render uses ConcurrentRoot + runWithDiscreteEvent + flushSyncWork + async queueMicrotask scheduler
- Test render uses act() + synchronous doRender() — this is why tests pass
- insertChar() calls Editor.insertText then forceRender() (setVersion(v+1))
- The state update should be flushed by reconciler.flushSyncWork() after handleChunk
- Either flushSyncWork fails to process the update, or the scheduler/incremental diff misses the change
- Debug logging was being added to trace the exact failure point when investigation was paused

title: Show focus outline when editing in columns/tabs/lists views
description: When editing a node in columns/tabs/lists view, show the focus outline (border). Layout shift from the outline appearing is acceptable. Currently the outline only shows when navigating, not when in edit mode.

title: Light blue focus ring for text edit mode across all editable fields
description:
Cyan border = 'you are typing here.' Reserved exclusively for active text input focus. No other UI element uses cyan borders.

**Card inline edit**: Card border → cyan when editing. (done)

**Column header edit**: Cyan BORDER (not blueBright background). Change current backgroundColor approach to border-based.

**Body block edit**: Cyan border appears when editing — even if block was previously borderless.

**Dialog input fields**: Search, NewItem, DatePrompt, ProjectPicker — input field area inside dialog gets cyan border. Dialog OUTER border must NOT be cyan — use neutral color (white/gray).

**Cyan exclusivity**: No non-editable UI element uses cyan border. Change ModalDialog default from cyan to neutral. Change HelpOverlay, DetailPane cyan borders to neutral.

title: Migrate km-tui inline editing to EditContext
description:
## Status: Partially Complete

### What was done (commits 0e05c8ae, 42edf41b)
- Removed Slate.js (-1537 lines)
- Created EditContext system in inkx (createTermEditContext + useEditContext hook + text-cursor.ts)
- Migrated all km-tui consumers to useEditContext: InlineEditField, SearchDialog, NewItemDialog, DatePromptDialog, ProjectPicker

### The question: We have TextArea in inkx — why just a hook?

**TextArea** (vendor/beorn-inkx/src/components/TextArea.tsx) is a self-contained component:
- Has its own input handling via useInput (NOT the command system)
- Renders multi-line text with word wrapping, scrolling, cursor display
- Works standalone — no command system integration

**useEditContext** (vendor/beorn-inkx/src/hooks/use-edit-context.ts) is a hook:
- Integrates with km-tui's command system via activeEditTargetRef/activeEditContextRef
- Provides EditTarget interface (insertChar, deleteBackward, cursorLeft, confirm, cancel, etc.)
- Supports onTextOp for undo logging, onSplitAtBoundary/onMergeBackward for tree ops
- Auto-save on unmount
- NO rendering — consumers render beforeCursor/afterCursor manually

**Why km-tui uses the hook, not TextArea:**
1. Command system: All keys route through keybinding layers → board-actions.ts → EditTarget methods. TextArea bypasses this entirely (uses useInput directly).
2. Custom rendering: Dialogs need custom prompts, colors, layout — not TextArea's fixed rendering.
3. Undo integration: useEditContext fires TextOp events for the undo stack.
4. Tree operations: onSplitAtBoundary/onMergeBackward connect text editing to document structure.

### What's missing (the actual gap)
useEditContext provides everything for **single-line** editing (titles, search, date input). For **multi-line body editing**, we need:
- Scroll viewport management (keep cursor visible in bounded area)
- Multi-line text display with cursor highlighting
- Visual line slicing (show lines[scrollOffset : scrollOffset + height])

### Remaining work
Create **EditContextDisplay** — a pure rendering component (~200-300 LOC) that:
1. Consumes useEditContext output (editContext, value, cursor)
2. Implements TextArea's scrolling + multi-line rendering logic (extracted)
3. Has NO input handling (relies on command system via EditTarget)
4. Used by a new BodyEditField component in km-tui for body block editing

TextArea stays unchanged (standalone use cases). useEditContext stays unchanged.

Files:
- vendor/beorn-inkx/src/components/EditContextDisplay.tsx (NEW ~150 LOC)
- apps/km-tui/src/views/BodyEditField.tsx (NEW ~40 LOC)
- vendor/beorn-inkx/src/index.ts (export new component)
notes: 2026-02-18: BodyEditField created and wired into TreeNode.tsx. Body blocks (p, code, quote) now use BodyEditField with EditContextDisplay for scroll viewport support. Title editing still uses InlineEditField. All 82 km-tui test files (1558 tests) pass.

title: Embedded links from km add show as \!link, ctrl-enter fails
description: After km add creates embed links, TUI shows raw \![[target]] syntax instead of resolved content. Ctrl-enter says 'not an embed'. Root cause: km add creates node with type:li+link_to, serializes as \![[target]], but file watcher re-parse creates type:link node with link_to:null. Link resolution may not re-run.
notes: TTY (0215a): Embeds in real vault still show ! prefix (e.g. '!2026 @Kaiser Getting Started Guide.pdf'). Screenshots confirm. Re-opening.

title: Embedded nodes still render with \! prefix after 'km add'
description: After using 'km add' to create embedded links, the nodes still render with the \! prefix (from \![[target]] syntax) in the TUI. See /tmp/vt/@next.

title: Embedded nodes: distinguish outline items vs body blocks for rendering
description:
Current embed rendering treats all embedded nodes the same way. But we need to distinguish between:
- Outline items (oi/li) — should render as cards/nodes (task items, sections)
- Body blocks (p, h, code, quote, etc.) — should render as inline content blocks
Example: embedded blocks in @next#inbox should render as blocks, not as outline items.
This is a design decision — needs discussion about the rendering model for different node types when embedded.

title: Embedded nodes show raw IDs instead of resolved content
description: Embed references \![[^sourceId]] in detail pane body show as raw short IDs (e.g., BKK8N7QA) instead of resolving to the target node's content. Likely link_to resolution not happening during parse, or body rendering not following link_to.
notes: Also seen in FAMILY SCHEDULE detail pane — bare block IDs visible alongside truncated title

title: Card content shows raw \!%5B%5B embed syntax
description: Cards display raw '\![%5B' prefix when content contains embed wikilinks (e.g., '\![%5Bfile.jpg]]'). The embed syntax should be resolved or stripped, not shown as-is. Visible on stabell/early-orbit board in 'Organize into boxes' card.
notes:
Re-investigated: fix from commit fe773e01 is on main. Three layers protect against ![[]] leak: (1) stripForDisplay in @km/tree, (2) InlineText parser, (3) parseToPlainText. All 9 tests pass. Remaining concern: cleanContentForDisplay in getDisplayContent does NOT strip embeds but relies on InlineText. Will check if there is a remaining gap in that path.
Defense-in-depth fix: Added inline embed stripping to cleanContentForDisplay() in TreeNode.tsx. This function is used in the getDisplayContent() path and was the only remaining code path that could return content with raw ![[...]] syntax. While InlineText handled it at render time, the raw string could leak through non-InlineText code paths. Also added alias variant test. Total: 10 tests in embed-syntax-leak.test.ts + 112 in display.test.ts all pass.

title: Column loading UX: show per-column loading indicator during file parse (5-10s)
description: When opening a large repo (imports/asana, 73 files), the board goes through 3 phases: 1) Loading indicator (OK), 2) Columns with headers but (empty) content for 5-10s while markdown files are parsed (NOT OK — looks broken), 3) Full content loaded (OK). Fix: show skeleton/loading indicator per column during phase 2 instead of (empty). The SkeletonCards component already exists — use it when column.cards.length === 0 and isLoading is true.
notes: Session 0218e: Root cause found. Two issues: (1) No .km/ in imports/asana — fixed with 'km init --repo imports/asana --force'. (2) Section files (#home.md etc.) contain embed refs (\![[^asanaId]]) to tasks that don't exist in the export. These are tag-based cross-references from Asana — the tag sections reference tasks that may belong to projects not in the export scope. After init+sync, 106k nodes loaded, board shows columns with cards but content shows short ID fallbacks like (01KHTAD5). This is actually the km-tui.bare-block-ids issue for dangling refs, not an empty columns issue. The original 'empty columns with 74 items' was the missing .km/ init.

title: Skip delete confirmation for completely empty nodes
description: When deleting a node (column or board) that is completely empty (no content, no children), skip the confirmation dialog. Empty nodes have no content worth protecting, so the confirmation is just friction.

title: Tasks show 'See <>' with missing link text in Asana import
description: Some imported Asana tasks display 'See <>' where a link should be. The link text/URL is missing. Check imports/asana/stabell/ source data and the inline component rendering pipeline. Likely a parser issue where the link node has no URL or text.
notes:
Root cause: Two-layer bug. (1) In inline-parser.ts, phrasingToInline() discarded blockRef/section fields from KmWikilink when converting to InlineNode, making [[^GID]] wikilinks produce empty targets. (2) In detail-pane-helpers.ts, stripKnownMentions() converted wikilinks to plain text via inlineNodesToPlainText(), which turned [[^GID]] into bare ^GID text. When that text was re-parsed by InlineText, the ^GID matched the standalone block ref regex and rendered as invisible metadata.

Fix: (A) inline-parser.ts: Reconstruct full target from KmWikilink parts (target + section + blockRef) so wikilinks always have visible targets. (B) detail-pane-helpers.ts: Add explicit wikilink case in stripKnownFromNodes() that preserves [[...]] brackets, preventing the text from being misinterpreted during re-parsing.

Tests: Updated 4 existing tests that expected empty wikilink targets. Added 2 new tests: parser test for angle-bracket block ref rendering, and TUI test verifying See <[[^GID]]> displays visible reference.

title: Event architecture: stale layout during batches, module-level state, unnecessary re-renders
description:
## Systematic Problems in the TUI Event Architecture

Root cause analysis from 12+ sessions (2026-02-06 through 2026-02-08) fighting visual bell flashes and cursoring bugs. The individual bugs were fixed, but the architecture has systematic issues that will create more bugs.

### Problem 1: Stale Layout During Event Batches (MEDIUM IMPACT)

When multiple keys arrive in one stdin read (auto-repeat), they're batched and processed by `processEventBatch()` without rendering between handlers. Each handler gets fresh store state via `get()`, but **layout is stale** because:
- `dispatchBoard()` updates `cursorNodeId` synchronously via Zustand `set()`
- But `updateLayout()` runs in a React `useEffect` in Board.tsx — only after `doRender()`
- So key 2 in a batch sees key 1's layout (stale `colIndex`/`cardIndex`)

**Impact**: Horizontal nav (h/l) reads `layout.colIndex` which doesn't update until after render. Vertical nav (j/k) reads `cursorNodeId` from `boardState` which IS fresh — that's why j/k mostly works but h/l is more fragile.

**Fix options**:
1. Compute layout synchronously in `dispatchBoard()` instead of in React effects
2. Accept layout-is-one-behind and make handlers use `boardState.cursorNodeId` + tree-walking instead of `layout`
3. Break batches: render between each key (slower but correct)

### Problem 2: Module-Level Mutable State (`inBoundaryStreak`)

The `inBoundaryStreak` flag in `board-app.ts` is a module-level `let`. It:
- Leaks between test instances (fixed with `resetBoundaryStreak()`)
- Would leak between multiple app instances (only one in production, but architecturally wrong)
- Can't be inspected or tested via the store

**Fix**: Move into the store as non-reactive metadata, or into a closure captured by `createBoardApp()`.

### Problem 3: Silent Layout Mutation

`updateLayout()` in `board-app-store.ts` directly mutates `_get()` fields without calling `set()`. This is intentional (avoids double-render) but:
- Violates Zustand's contract (external state mutation)
- Makes it impossible to subscribe to layout changes
- Creates timing bugs where reads may see stale or fresh layout depending on render cycle

**Fix**: Use a separate mutable ref alongside the store, or make layout a computed value derived from `cursorNodeId` + tree structure.

### Problem 4: Unnecessary Re-renders on Bell Clear

Every keypress where `bellState` was previously set calls `setUI({ bellState: null })`, which triggers a Zustand re-render cycle. During boundary suppression, this means:
- Key 1: bell fires (necessary render)
- Key 2: clears bell (unnecessary render) + suppresses new bell (no render needed)
- Key 3: no bell to clear (no render) — but already wasted a render on key 2

**Fix**: Let the 150ms auto-dismiss timer handle bell clearing. Don't clear in handleKey.

### Summary

These are all consequences of the same architectural tension: **the event handler is synchronous but layout is async (React effects)**. The workarounds (silent mutation, module-level flags, eager bell clears) each solve their immediate problem but create subtle timing bugs.

Long-term fix: make layout a synchronous derivation of `cursorNodeId` + tree structure, computed on-demand rather than stored and async-updated.
design:
## Architecture: Synchronous Layout + Single Source of Truth

### Current Architecture (as-is)

```
                  KEY PRESS
                     │
                     ▼
              handleKey() [board-app.ts]
                     │
                     ▼
           buildActionCtx(get, exit)           ← snapshots store.layout (may be stale)
                     │
                     ▼
        processKeyWithContext(input, key, ctx)  ← command system resolves keybinding
                     │
                     ▼
           handleCommandAction(ctx, action)    ← reads ctx.layout.columns[colIndex]
                     │
              ┌──────┴──────┐
              ▼             ▼
       dispatchBoard()   repo.mutate()
       (silent mutation   (addNode/moveNode/
        or Zustand set)    deleteNode)
              │             │
              ▼             ▼
     recomputeLayout()   repo.version++
     (silent mutation     repo.notify()
      on store)                │
              │                ▼
              ▼          useColumns() [React hook]
     store.layout =      useSyncExternalStore(repo)
       fresh layout            │
              │                ▼
              │          deriveColumnsFromRepo()
              │          deriveCursorPosition()
              │                │
              │                ▼
              │        updateLayout() [useEffect]
              │        (silent mutation on store)
              │                │
              └────────┬───────┘
                       ▼
                  NEXT KEY PRESS
                  reads get().layout
```

### Where State Lives (5 locations!)

1. **Zustand store** (`board-app-store.ts`):
   - `cursorNodeId`, `rootId`, `foldedNodes`, `collapsedNodes`, `moveMode`, etc.
   - `layout` (ColumnsLayout) — silently mutated, never triggers subscriber
   - `ui` (UIState) — proper Zustand set()

2. **CursorStore** (`cursor-store.ts`):
   - Separate pub/sub for cursor position
   - Updated by both `recomputeLayout()` and `Board.tsx useEffect`

3. **React hooks** (`Board.tsx`):
   - `useColumns()` → derives columns from repo
   - `useCursorPosition()` → derives colIndex/cardIndex
   - `useMemo(() => columnsLayout)` → builds ColumnsLayout
   - Pushes back to store via `updateLayout()` useEffect

4. **Module-level state**:
   - `_layoutRepoVersion` in `board-app-store.ts`
   - `_needsFlush` in `board-actions-edit.ts`
   - `chordTimer` in `board-app.ts`
   - `lastKeyTime` in `board-app.ts`
   - `cardsViewNavigation` singleton in `board-app.ts`

5. **ActionCtx snapshot** (`tui-context.ts`):
   - Frozen snapshot of store state, built once per key event
   - `ctx.layout`, `ctx.column`, `ctx.card` — stale if repo mutated mid-handler
   - `ctx.repo` — live reference (mutations visible immediately)

### Root Causes of Bugs

1. **Dual derivation paths**: Layout is derived BOTH synchronously in `recomputeLayout()` (for key handler) AND asynchronously in React hooks (for rendering). These can disagree.

2. **Silent mutation breaks Zustand contract**: `recomputeLayout()` and `updateLayout()` both mutate `get()` directly. Components that select `layout` from the store won't re-render on changes.

3. **ActionCtx is a snapshot, but repo is live**: `buildActionCtx()` captures `layout.columns` at key-event start. After `repo.moveNode()`, `ctx.layout.columns[i].node.parent_idx` is stale because `recomputeLayout()` creates new column objects. The col-shift bug was exactly this.

4. **CursorStore synced from two places**: Both `recomputeLayout()` and `Board.tsx useEffect` call `cursorStore.setState()`. Race conditions between sync and async paths.

5. **refreshBoardState() re-derives columns**: After mutations, `refreshBoardState()` calls `deriveColumnsFromRepo()` again to find the new cursor target — a third derivation path.

### Design Principles

**Principle 1: Single derivation path.** Layout is derived in exactly one place, from exactly one source of truth.

**Principle 2: Synchronous by default.** Key handlers see consistent state. No "layout will be ready after the next render."

**Principle 3: No silent mutation.** Every state change goes through a proper setter. Subscribers are notified.

**Principle 4: Scoped state.** No module-level mutable state. All mutable state is owned by a factory closure or store.

**Principle 5: ActionCtx re-derived after mutations.** After a repo mutation, fresh layout is available immediately without re-snapshotting.

### Prior Art

- **ProseMirror**: `EditorState` is immutable. Transactions produce a new state synchronously. View reads the latest state for rendering. No dual derivation.
- **SlateJS**: Operations applied to `Editor` synchronously. React reads `editor.children` directly. Normalization runs inline.
- **Redux + Reselect**: Selectors derive state on read. No stored derived state. Memoization prevents redundant computation.
- **Zustand middleware**: `subscribeWithSelector` can compute derived state inline with `set()`.
- **Game loops**: Input → Update → Render. Each frame sees consistent state. No async gaps.

### Proposed Architecture

```
                  KEY PRESS
                     │
                     ▼
              handleKey() [board-app.ts]
                     │
                     ▼
      ┌─── store.dispatch(command) ───┐
      │                               │
      │  1. Resolve keybinding        │
      │  2. Execute action            │
      │     (may call repo.mutate)    │
      │  3. Recompute layout inline   │
      │  4. Single set() call         │
      │     with ALL changes          │
      └──────────────┬────────────────┘
                     │
                     ▼
              Zustand notifies
              subscribers
                     │
                     ▼
              Board renders
              (reads layout from store
               — no useColumns/useEffect
               derivation loop)
```

**Key changes:**

1. **Layout is a Zustand-computed selector** (or computed inline in set()). `deriveColumnsFromRepo()` + `deriveCursorPosition()` runs inside the store's `set()` callback, producing layout as part of the state update.

2. **No React-side derivation loop.** Board.tsx reads `store.layout` directly — no useColumns, no useCursorPosition, no updateLayout useEffect. React is a pure view layer.

3. **ActionCtx reads layout lazily.** Instead of snapshotting layout at key-event start, `ctx.layout` is a getter that calls `get().layout`. After any mutation + recompute, the next read sees fresh data.

4. **CursorStore updated inside set().** Single update point, synchronized with layout derivation. No dual-sync race.

5. **Module-level state moved into store or factory closure.** `_layoutRepoVersion` becomes a store field. `_needsFlush`, `chordTimer`, `lastKeyTime` become closure variables in `createBoardApp()`.

### Incremental Migration Steps

Each step is independently shippable and testable. Steps are ordered by risk (lowest first).

#### Step 1: Move module-level state into factory closures [LOW RISK]

Move `_layoutRepoVersion`, `_needsFlush`, `chordTimer`, `lastKeyTime` from module scope into the `createBoardApp()` / `createBoardAppStoreState()` closures.

**What changes**: board-app.ts, board-app-store.ts, board-actions-edit.ts
**What breaks if wrong**: Test isolation issues (already partially broken today)
**Validation**: Existing tests pass. Multiple board instances don't share state.

#### Step 2: Make recomputeLayout use set() instead of silent mutation [MEDIUM RISK]

Change `recomputeLayout()` to call `set({ layout, selectedNode, selectionLevel })` instead of mutating `get()` directly. This makes layout changes visible to Zustand subscribers.

The current double-render concern is addressed by batching: the cursor change and layout recompute happen in a single `set()` call (or consecutive calls that Zustand batches within the same synchronous tick).

**What changes**: board-app-store.ts (recomputeLayout, SELECT fast path, updateLayout)
**What breaks if wrong**: Extra re-renders. Performance regression on j/k.
**Validation**: Perf benchmarks (j/k < 5ms). Visual bell doesn't double-flash.
**Mitigation**: If performance regresses, use `subscribeWithSelector` to make Board only re-render on fields it uses. The CursorStore already handles most cursor-move cases without Board re-render.

#### Step 3: Eliminate React-side layout derivation (remove useColumns from Board) [MEDIUM RISK]

Board.tsx stops deriving layout. Instead:
- Board reads `store.layout` directly (already available from Step 2)
- Remove `useColumns()`, `useCursorPosition()`, `buildNodeIndex()` calls from Board.tsx
- Remove the `updateLayout()` useEffect feedback loop
- Keep `deriveColumnsFromRepo()` and `deriveCursorPosition()` as pure functions (used by store)

Board.tsx goes from ~200 lines of hook logic to ~20 lines of selector reads.

**What changes**: Board.tsx, board-app-store.ts
**What breaks if wrong**: Stale columns after repo mutations (file watcher sync). Repo subscription must trigger store recompute.
**Validation**: Hold j/k with rapid auto-repeat. File watcher sync updates board. Column shift works without stale references.
**Mitigation**: Add a repo.subscribe listener in the store that triggers recomputeLayout on external mutations (file watcher).

#### Step 4: Make ActionCtx lazy (getter-based layout access) [LOW RISK]

Change `buildActionCtx()` so `ctx.layout`, `ctx.column`, `ctx.card` are getters that read `get().layout` on each access. After a repo mutation + recompute within the same handler, subsequent reads see fresh data.

This eliminates the class of bugs where `ctx.layout` is stale mid-handler (like the col-shift bug).

**What changes**: board-app.ts (buildActionCtx), tui-context.ts (ActionCtx type)
**What breaks if wrong**: Performance (getter overhead). Should be negligible.
**Validation**: moveColumn test (the col-shift regression test). All board-edit tests.

#### Step 5: React-side subscription for external mutations [LOW RISK]

Repo mutations from external sources (file watcher, sync) need to trigger layout recompute. Add `repo.subscribe()` in the store factory that calls `recomputeLayout()` when version changes AND the mutation wasn't initiated by a key handler.

**What changes**: board-app-store.ts (store factory adds repo subscription)
**What breaks if wrong**: Double recompute on key-handler mutations. Guard with "in handler" flag.
**Validation**: Edit a markdown file externally, verify board updates. Run watcher sync tests.

#### Step 6: Simplify CursorStore usage [LOW RISK, OPTIONAL]

After Steps 2-3, CursorStore is updated in exactly one place (inside `set()` via recomputeLayout). Consider whether CursorStore is still needed or can be replaced by Zustand selectors with `subscribeWithSelector`.

**What changes**: cursor-store.ts, cursor-context.tsx, Board.tsx, CardColumn.tsx
**Decision point**: If CursorStore's 2-card-re-render performance advantage matters, keep it. If Zustand selectors are fast enough, remove it.

#### Step 7: Remove structural sharing from useColumns [LOW RISK, DEFERRED]

After Step 3, `useColumns()` is no longer called in Board.tsx. If it's still used elsewhere, consider whether structural sharing is worth the complexity. If `deriveColumnsFromRepo()` is only called from the store (Step 3), structural sharing can be removed — the store already has referential stability through Zustand's shallow equality.

### Risk Assessment

| Step | Risk | Impact if Wrong | Rollback |
|------|------|-----------------|----------|
| 1. Module-level state → closure | Low | Test isolation | Revert 1 file |
| 2. Silent mutation → set() | Medium | Extra re-renders | Revert recomputeLayout changes |
| 3. Remove React derivation | Medium | Stale after file watcher | Revert Board.tsx changes |
| 4. Lazy ActionCtx | Low | Negligible perf cost | Revert buildActionCtx |
| 5. External mutation subscription | Low | Double recompute | Add guard flag |
| 6. Simplify CursorStore | Low | Minor perf change | Keep CursorStore |
| 7. Remove structural sharing | Low | Minor perf change | Keep sharing |

### What NOT to Change

- **Repo interface** (subscribe/getSnapshot) — already correct, used by useSyncExternalStore
- **Command system** (keybindings, command resolution) — orthogonal to state management
- **ViewNavigation** (directional resolution) — operates on repo, not layout
- **UndoStack/UndoableRepo** — correctly scoped, no state management issues
- **Tree/Parser/Filesystem layers** — below the architecture boundary

### Success Criteria

1. **No stale references**: After any repo mutation in a key handler, reading layout gives fresh data
2. **Single derivation path**: `deriveColumnsFromRepo()` called from exactly one place
3. **No silent mutations**: Every store state change goes through `set()`
4. **No module-level mutable state**: All state in store or factory closures
5. **Performance maintained**: j/k < 5ms, h/l < 10ms, rapid auto-repeat smooth
6. **Board.tsx simplified**: No useColumns, no updateLayout useEffect, no derivation loop
notes:
2026-02-18 deeper analysis of Problem 1 (stale layout):

The core navigation (viewNavigation.navigate) already uses fresh cursorNodeId + tree-walking, NOT stale layout. The stale layout issue is limited to stickyY visual measurement (navigator.getItemMidY reads rendered card positions). During batched h/l presses, the second l reads stale mid-Y from the previous render.

navStateFrom(ctx) is CLEAN — uses cursorNodeId, rootId, foldedNodes, collapsedNodes (all fresh from store).

Impact: stickyY capture is approximate during rapid h/l presses. This causes curswantY test failures but doesn't break navigation logic.

Fix options analyzed:
1. Force render between batch keys — correct but slow (defeats batching)
2. Compute stickyY from tree structure — loses visual accuracy (card heights vary)
3. Defer stickyY capture to after render — needs architecture change (stickyY capture in useEffect)
4. Accept as is — stickyY is a hint, not exact. Rapid h/l navigation still works, just slightly imprecise Y positioning.

Recommendation: Option 3 (defer stickyY capture to post-render) is the cleanest fix but requires refactoring how navigator.setStickyY integrates with the React render cycle.

The focus system infrastructure is 100% complete in inkx, but the km-tui render tree hasn't been decorated with focus props. Everything operates in fallback/compatibility mode.

## Current state (transitional shims)

1. **Virtual focus with fake nodes** (driver.ts:286-300) — ctx.focus('board-area') creates fake {props:{testID}, children:[], parent:null} objects and passes them with `as any`. No real DOM node is focused.

3. **CardColumn `|| activeId \!== 'detail-pane'` fallback** (CardColumn.tsx:171,610) — useFocusWithin('board-area') always returns false. Falls back to string comparison.

4. **No focusable/testID props** in the render tree — zero occurrences of `focusable` in views/.

## Tasks

1. Add `testID='board-area' focusable` to board area Box in Board.tsx
2. Add `testID='detail-pane' focusable` to detail pane wrapper Box
3. Remove `focused` prop from DetailPane — let useFocusable() be sole source
4. Remove `|| fallback` patterns in CardColumn
5. Remove getFakeNode / virtual focus hack in driver.ts — use focusManager.focusById() instead
6. Update tests that pass focused prop or check focusedPane
7. InputLayerProvider stays (different concern from focusScope — see notes)

## InputLayerProvider analysis

InputLayerProvider is NOT redundant with focusScope. They solve different problems:
- **focusScope** = Tab traversal boundary (where can Tab go next?)
- **InputLayerProvider** = key handler isolation stack (who processes this keypress?)

The command system operates at the `term:key` level (before DOM event dispatch). InputLayerProvider intercepts keys at that level. For focusScope/onKeyDown to replace it, the entire command system would need to migrate from term:key to component-level onKeyDown — that's a separate, larger migration (future phase).

title: Discuss: integrate focusScope with InputLayerProvider
description:
## Architecture: TEA + React Event Coexistence

### Goal
Support both centralized TEA control AND component-local React event handling.

### Design

```
terminal input
  → hightea dispatches to focused node (onKeyDown)
  → event bubbles up through focusScopes
  → if no component calls stopPropagation...
  → reaches the root scope
  → TEA dispatcher (command system) handles it
```

- **focusScope** = event routing layer (React side). Component authors write `<Box onKeyDown={...}>`.
- **TEA command system** = root-level catchall. App-wide keybindings (j/k, etc.) registered centrally.
- **InputLayerProvider** = transitional shim. Today events don't flow through React at all — InputLayerProvider intercepts at term:key level BEFORE the React tree. Once events flow through focusScope, InputLayerProvider is redundant.

### Why This Works
- React component authors get normal `onKeyDown` — no framework to learn
- TEA/app authors get centralized dispatch — predictable, testable
- focusScope boundaries provide natural isolation (dialog scope = keys don't leak)
- No dual system — one event flow, two consumption points

### Migration Order
1. **Dialogs** — dialog IS a focusScope, key handling IS component-local. Easiest win.
2. **Text input** — inline edit already wants component-local onKeyDown
3. **Command system** — becomes root onKeyDown handler instead of term:key interceptor
4. **Remove InputLayerProvider** — nothing uses it anymore

### Status
Design discussion — agreed on direction. Implementation is Phase 5+ per TEA roadmap.
notes:
## Argument: focusScope should NOT integrate with InputLayerProvider for non-keyboard events

### Core distinction
- focusScope: tree model, spatial (React tree structure), targets specific focused node
- InputLayerProvider: stack model (LIFO), temporal (mount order), targets whoever registered last

### 5 reasons to keep them separate:

1. **Mouse events need spatial targeting, not stack ordering.** Mouse events hit a point on screen via hitTest() against the layout tree. InputLayerProvider's LIFO stack has no spatial position concept. You'd re-implement hit testing inside every handler.

2. **Non-keyboard events don't consume like keyboard events.** InputLayerProvider's true/false consumption model works for keys (one handler responds). Mouse events bubble via DOM semantics — onClick bubbles, onWheel goes to scroll containers, onMouseEnter is non-bubbling. These already work via node tree + stopPropagation().

3. **focusScope = focus isolation, not event routing.** focusScope constrains Tab cycling within a subtree (dialog). It has nothing to do with mouse events. You should be able to click OUTSIDE a focusScope to close the dialog — trapping mouse events would be the opposite of expected behavior.

4. **InputLayerProvider is transitional; focusScope is permanent.** InputLayerProvider exists because inkx originally had no DOM-like event dispatch. It has fundamental flaws (registration order depends on React commit timing, no layout relationship, no introspection). focusScope fixes keyboard; extending it to non-keyboard would mean reinventing the DOM event model.

5. **Current architecture already handles this.** Mouse: hitTest → deepest node → bubble. Keyboard: focused node → bubble. Both use the same node tree and stopPropagation(). Neither needs InputLayerProvider or focusScope for dispatch.

### Right boundary
- focusScope = Focus containment (Tab cycling, Escape exits scope)
- Node tree = Event dispatch (hitTest for mouse, focused node for keyboard, bubbling for both)
- InputLayerProvider = Legacy shim, replaced by node-tree dispatch once focus system wired

## Deep Research: Cross-Framework Analysis (O3 Deep Research, 2026-02-21)

**Universal finding**: ALL major UI frameworks (React DOM, React Native, Flutter, SwiftUI, WPF, Qt, Android) separate keyboard focus from pointer event dispatch. No framework couples focus scopes with non-keyboard events.

Key findings:
- Flutter FocusScope: restricts Tab/arrow only, pointer events hit-test independently
- WPF FocusManager: keyboard focus + logical focus (memory), no mouse coupling  
- Qt FocusScope: QML key routing only, MouseArea is independent
- Web: inert/showModal() are SEPARATE mechanisms from focus
- Android: touch mode removes focus highlights, touch bypasses all focus

The only 'coupling' anywhere is modal dialogs — and those use SEPARATE APIs (inert, ModalBarrier, ShowDialog, modal popups) — not focus scope features.

Our architecture matches industry consensus exactly:
- focusScope = focus containment (Tab/arrow)
- Node tree + hitTest = pointer dispatch
- InputLayerProvider = transitional (being removed)
- Modal dialogs = separate mechanism (future)

Full report: /tmp/llm-d3a7049b-1771722050282-85hy.txt

title: Screen garbles on cursor movement with large Asana vault (256k nodes)

title: Editing HR stops keyboard input; HR not converted to editable '---' card

**Parser preserves raw content**: ast2nodes.ts stores raw thematic break text (---, ***, ___, etc.) in node.content.

**Serializer uses stored content**: nodes2md.ts outputs node.content ?? '---' for HR nodes (roundtrip fidelity).

**Display (not editing)**: HR content centered with SPACES (no decorative dash line). Just the text content padded with spaces. Yellow when selected, dimmed otherwise. Height: 1 row, no border.

**Display (editing)**: Normal bordered card with cyan border (focus ring), inline edit field pre-filled with stored content.

**Type conversion (→ hr)**: On save, if trimmed content matches valid HR pattern and node type is p/li, convert type to hr.

**Type conversion (→ p)**: On save, if content no longer matches HR pattern and node type is hr, convert type to p.

**Valid HR patterns**: At minimum: ---, ***, ___ (3+ of same char). Shared regex.
notes: TTY verification (2026-02-16): HR editing looks clean in real terminal — cyan border, '---' content with block cursor, NO blue background fill. User's earlier screenshot was from before the fix. Buffer test added checking only 1 inverse cell (cursor char) on the edit row.

title: Cursoring to partially visible columns doesn't trigger horizontal scroll
description:
When navigating right to a column that requires horizontal scrolling, the cursor column's right edge extends exactly 1 character past the viewport boundary at certain viewport widths. The rightmost character of the column is clipped/invisible.

Confirmed failing widths (3 columns): 60, 65, 73, 75, 77, 85.
Confirmed passing widths: 70, 72, 74, 76, 78, 80, 90.

Root cause: The estimatedVisibleCount in useVirtualization (line 162) uses Math.ceil which overcounts visible items. With overflow indicators reserving 2 chars (effectiveViewport = width - 2), the scroll algorithm places items such that their total physical width (items + gaps) exceeds the effective viewport by 1 char.

Example at width=73: expandedWidth=36, gap=1, effectiveViewport=71. Two items + gap = 36+1+36 = 73 > 71. But estimatedVisibleCount=ceil(71/37)=2, so calcEdgeBasedScrollOffset thinks 2 items fit.

Fix is in vendor/beorn-inkx/src/hooks/useVirtualization.ts or scroll-utils.ts — the visible count estimation needs to account for the actual physical width of items + gaps, not just item count.
notes: inkx fix committed 9d122e9: calcItemOverflow calculates actual indicator overhead per-edge, bumps displayScrollOffset+1 when overflow detected. Tests in hscroll-partial.test.ts. Needs user verification.

notes:
Root cause found (agent afe8ad0): 1. ITEM SPLITTING: Asana html_notes uses

/

tags → turndown converts to # Heading markdown → when km re-parses, headings create new sections. Fix: escape heading syntax in body content before storing as p node, OR configure turndown to convert headings to **bold** instead of ATX. 2. BODY TEXT RUNS TOGETHER: DetailPane.tsx BodyBlock filters empty lines: content.split('\n').filter(l => l.trim() !== ''). This removes paragraph breaks. Also preprocessAsanaHtml collapses double
to single. Fix: preserve blank lines as visual spacers. 3. ATTACHMENTS AS TRUNCATED IDS: parser.ts nodeToText() doesn't handle mdast image nodes (no value/children). Returns '' → getNodeDisplayName falls back to (ULID prefix). Fix: handle image nodes in nodeToText: return node.alt or ![alt](url). 4. Fixed both issues: (1) Added custom turndown rule in asana-types.ts to convert HTML headings to bold text instead of ATX headings, preventing km parser from splitting task descriptions into separate items. title: TUI: 'j' from Kaiser Health in @next.md#inbox jumps cursor to board title
description: Navigating down ('j') in @next.md#inbox from the 'Kaiser Health' card causes the cursor to jump to the board title instead of the next card. Possible regression from km-tui.virtual-nav fix (40f8a894) or uncovered variant of km-tui-cursor-jump.
notes:
Investigation (2026-02-15): Extensive code analysis and testing. Could NOT reproduce the bug.

## What was tested
1. **Unit test on view-navigation**: `navigate("down")` from a link-type embed (Kaiser Health equivalent) correctly returns the next sibling card ID
2. **nodeIndex verification**: link-type embed nodes correctly appear in buildNodeIndex() with proper cardIndex
3. **Full rendering pipeline (68 cards)**: j navigates through all 68 mixed p/link embed cards without jumping to board
4. **Focused test (position 9)**: j from link-type embed at position 9 goes to next card correctly
5. **Real vault /tmp/vt**: Both navigate-down and full rendering pipeline work correctly with real data

## Code path traced
- handleCursorMove → handleVerticalNav → viewNavigation.navigate("down") → getSibling()
- getSibling uses repo.getChildren(parent_id) + indexOfChild for O(1) sibling lookup
- SELECT fast path uses nodeIndex.get(nodeId) — if not found, falls to selectionLevel="board" (the symptom)
- deriveColumnsFromRepo correctly includes type="link" nodes as body cards
- buildNodeIndex correctly maps all body cards including type="link"

## Hypothesis
The bug may be timing-related: if a file watcher mutation invalidates the repo snapshot between navigate() returning a valid target and the SELECT action looking it up in nodeIndex, the _layoutRepoVersion check in board-app-store.ts would trigger a full recompute with potentially stale columns. This is speculative — the static navigation logic is correct.

## Test file created
apps/km-tui/tests/inbox-cursor-jump.test.ts — 6 tests, all passing. Provides regression coverage for mixed p/link embed navigation in large columns.

Shift+Tab already does structural outdent correctly via outdentNode(). Need: 1) New indent command + handler that reparents under prev sibling, 2) Rewire Tab binding from shift_right to indent.

title: Undo/redo support for indent/outdent operations

title: Replace regex text pipeline with inline AST → JSX rendering
description:
Replace regex text pipeline with inline AST → JSX rendering.

## Status: Ready to implement

All infrastructure is BUILT (zero consumers):
- `inline-parser.ts` — mdast-based parser (`parseInlineText()`), 30+ tests passing
- `InlineComponents.tsx` — 13 JSX components + `InlineText` drop-in + `InlineRenderContext`
- `inline-ast-types.ts` — 13 InlineNode types

## Migration Plan (6 phases)

2. **JSX consumers** — shared-components.tsx (1), NodeView.tsx (6), DetailPane.tsx (9 sites)
