title: Inline AST cleanup: eliminate stripForDisplay and stripFgColor holdovers
description:
## Goal
Complete the inline AST migration by eliminating remaining old-system holdovers.

## Tasks

### 1. Eliminate stripForDisplay() from views
`stripForDisplay()` (from @km/tree) pre-processes DB content before `<InlineText>`. The inline parser already handles block refs and fields, but:
- Fields render as styled `key:: value` instead of being stripped (card titles don't want this)
- Arrow refs `→ ^numericId` are partially handled (^id becomes blockref, but `→ ` stays)

**Fix**: The InlineRenderContext already has `stripRefs` — but we also need fields to render as empty in card title contexts. Either:
- Add field nodes to blockref-like "render empty" behavior when a context flag is set
- Or have stripForDisplay's work absorbed into the parser's km-syntax handling

Sites: TreeNode.tsx (2), NodeView.tsx (4), render.ts (1)

### 2. Eliminate stripFgColor() from views  
`stripFgColor()` strips ANSI fg colors from `infoSuffix` and `dateBadge` — pre-formatted ANSI badge strings.

**Fix**: Convert badge rendering from ANSI string construction to React components. Then selection highlighting works via `noColor` context or parent `<Text color={...}>` inheritance.

Sites: TreeNode.tsx (2), NodeView.tsx (2)

### 3. Clean up rich.ts
After #1 and #2:
- `stripFgColor` may become unused → delete
- `displayLength` is a thin wrapper around `string-width` → evaluate if still needed or consolidate
- If rich.ts becomes empty, delete it and update index.ts

### 4. Asana re-fetch (manual step, not code)
Cached JSON still has old Turndown output. Re-fetch to get clean HTML→mdast conversions:
```
bun km import asana --workspace Stabell --fetch --fetch-restart
bun km import asana --workspace Stabell --import --force
```

title: Leverage full Kitty + mouse input in km TUI
description:
With inkx now supporting full Kitty protocol and SGR mouse, wire these into km TUI for a dramatically better input experience.

## Keyboard (Kitty protocol)

- **Cmd+hjkl** for node shifting — DONE (km-infra.kitty-proto), works on Ghostty
- **Cmd+Z/Cmd+Shift+Z** — native undo/redo (currently Alt+u/Alt+r workaround)
- **Cmd+S** — save/sync (currently no shortcut)
- **Cmd+F** — search/filter (currently /)
- **Cmd+Enter** — create sibling, **Cmd+Shift+Enter** — create child
- **Key repeat events** — smooth continuous scroll when holding j/k (currently discrete)
- **Key release events** — hold Space to peek detail pane, release to dismiss
- **Option aliases** — keybindings accept opt/cmd as aliases for meta/super
- **Auto-detection** — Kitty protocol enabled automatically, graceful fallback on legacy terminals

## Mouse

- **Click** on card/node → select (move cursor to that item)
- **Click** on fold toggle (▸/▾) → expand/collapse
- **Click** on column header → focus column
- **Ctrl+Click** → multi-select nodes
- **Cmd+Click** on URL → open in browser
- **Scroll wheel** in columns → scroll the column
- **Scroll wheel** in detail pane → scroll detail content
- **Drag** (future) → reorder nodes

## Hit Registry Integration

Wire the existing HitRegistry into km TUI components:
- TreeNode registers click regions for each node
- CardColumn registers scroll areas and headers
- DetailPane registers its scroll area
- Dialog/modal components register at higher z-index

## Implementation Notes

Depends on inkx Kitty + mouse runtime wiring being complete (km-silvery-legacy.kitty-auto, km-silvery-legacy.mouse-runtime).
The command system already supports super modifier — this is about wiring mouse events and adding new Cmd+ shortcuts.

title: Global input mode state machine with push/pop context stack
description: O3 recommendation: Implement a global keyboard mode manager using a context stack pattern. States: 'command', 'insert', 'dialog:search', 'dialog:rename', etc. Push/pop model — opening any dialog pushes its mode, closing pops back to previous. Single source of truth for 'who handles keystrokes right now'. Prevents the entire category of bugs where two subsystems both process the same key event (keys-as-text, search close focus leak, edit mode after zoom). Related: km-tui.keys-as-text (this is the architectural fix).
notes: O3 deep research (0218e): Recommends context stack pattern: [BoardCommandsContext] → push SearchDialogContext on open → pop on close. Makes it structurally impossible for two contexts to handle same keystroke. States: command, insert, dialog:search, dialog:rename, etc. This is the architectural foundation that prevents the entire category of keys-as-text bugs.

title: Internal link navigation (km:// wiki/block refs)
description: Wiki links and block refs now emit OSC 8 hyperlinks with km://wiki/ and km://block/ schemes. Add onClick handlers to navigate to the linked node when clicked. This enables mouse-driven navigation between linked notes/blocks in the TUI.

title: J/K block navigation is stub — should drill into/out of cards
description: J/K (uppercase) are bound to block_nav_down/block_nav_up but board-actions-nav.ts:52 says: 'block_up/block_down are stubs that map to regular up/down for now (TODO: auto-unfold + block jump)'. Expected: J on a card selects first subitem (drills in), K backs out. Actual: J/K just move to next/prev sibling card (same as j/k).
notes:
Decker reference (decker-dragaboard/src/commands/cursoring.ts):
- '>' = goIn() — drill into first child (structural descent), auto-unfold if folded
- '<' = goOut() — jump to parent (structural ascent)
- hjkl = visual navigation within current level
- Pattern: structural nav checks for children first, if none + folded → unfold as side effect, else fallback to visual nav

km approach: J should = drill in (select first child of card), auto-unfold if folded. K should = drill out (back to parent). This maps to Decker's >/< but on J/K. Current j/k (lowercase) stays as visual cursor movement.

title: Navigation keys captured as text input on card title — data corruption
description: In TTY exploration: pressing j on selected card appends 'j' to title (renamed 'Archive' to 'Archivej' on disk). Enter creates new card instead of zooming. Keys go to title editing instead of command navigation. MAY be TTY tool artifact — needs TUI test verification. If real, this is P1 data corruption. Vault: /tmp/vt. Screenshot: /tmp/explore-screenshots/11-tasks-detail.png
notes:
Repro confirmed 0218e: During search, typed 'fix rap sheet greg fbi blah'. Search apparently closed mid-typing (when query yielded no results?) and remaining keystrokes went into editing a card title — created a card '□ sheet greg fbi blahhhh' in the Next Bjørn section. This is the same P1 keys-as-text bug: search dialog closure doesn't properly restore keyboard mode, so subsequent keystrokes go to card editing instead of commands.
O3 deep research diagnosis: Classic focus-management issue. (1) Enter key propagation — handleSearchSelect closes dialog + dispatches ZOOM_IN, same Enter keystroke propagates to newly-focused card, triggering edit mode. (2) No mode restore — closing search doesn't explicitly set mode back to 'command'. Fix: stopPropagation on Enter when closing search dialog, or setTimeout(...,0) to defer board focus. Architectural fix: global keyboard mode manager with context stack (push SearchDialogContext, pop on close).
O3 deep research diagnosis (0218e): Enter key propagation is the likely mechanism. User presses Enter to select search result → handleSearchSelect closes dialog + dispatches ZOOM_IN → board re-renders with target card selected → same Enter keystroke propagates to newly-focused card, triggering edit mode → subsequent j/k go to text editor. Two-part fix: (A) Immediate: stopPropagation or setTimeout(..., 0) to defer board focus by one tick. (B) Architectural: input mode context stack (see km-tui.input-mode-stack). Include viaSearch=true flag in ZOOM_IN so card component knows not to auto-focus text editor.
O3 deep research (session 0218e): Classic focus-management issue. Enter key from search dialog propagates to newly-focused card, triggering edit mode. Fix: (1) Immediate: stopPropagation on Enter or setTimeout(...,0) defer. (2) Architectural: Global keyboard mode stack — see km-tui.input-mode-stack. (3) Add viaSearch=true flag to ZOOM_IN so card component doesn't auto-focus text editor.

title: Slim down InitialBoardData — remove dead fields, keep as UI state bundle
description: InitialBoardData (formerly TUIBoardState) is useful as a bundled UI state type. But it currently has dead fields that are always hardcoded (visualMode, searchMode, helpMode, selectedNodes, searchQuery). Slim it to only live fields: rootId, rootPath, columns, collapsedColumns, collapsedNodeIds, foldedNodes. Keep as a single prop for passing UI state. Already partially done in commit 4f814dac (renamed + some fields removed). Verify no dead fields remain.

title: Level 1: Board useInput → useInputLayer migration
description:
Migrate Board.tsx from direct useInput to useInputLayer("board") as the base input layer.

## Current State
- Board.tsx line 872 uses `useInput()` directly for ALL key handling
- Dialogs (SearchDialog, ProjectPicker, NewItemDialog) already use `useInputLayer()`
- InputLayerProvider wraps BoardApp in tui.tsx line 192
- Board's useInput and dialogs's useInputLayer coexist but Board bypasses the layer stack

## Problem
Board's `useInput` fires independently of the InputLayerProvider stack. When a dialog is open, BOTH the dialog's useInputLayer handler AND Board's useInput fire, causing potential double-handling.

## Target
- Board uses `useInputLayer("board", handler)` as the base layer
- Handler returns `true` to consume (always — Board is the bottom layer)
- Dialogs consume keys before Board via stack ordering
- Single unified input path through InputLayerProvider

## Files to Modify
- `apps/km-tui/src/views/Board.tsx` — `useInput` → `useInputLayer`
- `apps/km-tui/src/views/board-input.ts` — handler returns boolean (consumed?)

## Testing
- Existing driver tests should pass unchanged
- Verify dialogs consume keys (escape, typing) without Board also handling them

title: Level 2: Migrate Board state to createApp() + Zustand store
description:
Replace Board's useReducer with Zustand store via createApp(). Board becomes pure view.

## Current State
- Board.tsx owns state via `useReducer` (TUIBoardState, UIState, BoardState)
- Driver accesses state via `onStateCapture` callback workaround
- Interface named `BoardCapturedState_REPLACE_WITH_CREATEAPP_STORE` (flagged as temporary)
- driver.ts line 213: "WORKAROUND: Replace this driver with createApp()"

## Target
- New `apps/km-tui/src/board-app.ts` defines createApp() with Zustand store
- Board becomes pure view: `useApp(selector)` instead of useReducer
- Driver accesses `app.store.getState()` directly — no callback hack
- Key handling remains in useInputLayer (from L1) for now

## Compatibility Issue
createApp() currently does NOT wrap with InputLayerProvider. To make L2 work while keeping useInputLayer from L1:
- Option A: Extend createApp() to accept custom providers (add InputLayerProvider)
- Option B: createApp() provides store only, key handling stays in useInputLayer
- Option C: Move InputLayerProvider inside createApp() as standard feature in inkx

Prefer Option C — InputLayerProvider should be standard in createApp().

## Files to Modify
- `vendor/beorn-inkx/src/runtime/create-app.tsx` — add InputLayerProvider to wrapped element
- `apps/km-tui/src/board-app.ts` (new) — createApp() definition with store factory
- `apps/km-tui/src/views/Board.tsx` — useReducer → useApp(selector)
- `apps/km-tui/src/driver.ts` — app.store.getState() instead of onStateCapture
- Remove `BoardCapturedState_REPLACE_WITH_CREATEAPP_STORE` interface

## Dependencies
- Requires L1 (Board on useInputLayer) first

title: Level 3: Centralize key handling in createApp() term:key handler
description:
Move ALL key handling from useInputLayer to createApp() centralized term:key handler.

## Current State (after L2)
- Board state in Zustand store via createApp()
- Keys still flow through useInputLayer → command bridge → command system
- InputLayerProvider still manages input dispatch

## Target
- createApp() term:key handler receives ALL keys before React
- Handler calls processKeyWithContext → command system → when predicates → action
- Actions update Zustand store via set()
- React re-renders via useApp(selector) subscriptions
- No useInputLayer, no InputLayerProvider needed

## Key Flow
```
stdin → TermProvider → term:key event → createApp handler
  → processKeyWithContext → @km/commands (when predicates)
  → action → set() Zustand store
  → React re-renders via useApp(selector)
```

## Dialog Input
Dialogs (search, new item, project picker) handled via when predicates:
- `when: textInputFocused` routes to TextEditTarget
- `when: isInlineEditing` routes to inline edit
- Dialog-specific keys (Escape, Enter) use dialog-specific predicates
- No per-dialog useInputLayer handlers needed

## Advantages
- Keys handled before React render cycle
- Single entry point for all input
- No race conditions from async useEffect registration
- Testable: driver.press() → term:key → same path as live app
- AI introspection: app.getState() gives full picture

## Files to Modify
- `apps/km-tui/src/board-app.ts` — add term:key handler
- `apps/km-tui/src/views/Board.tsx` — remove useInputLayer
- `apps/km-tui/src/views/SearchDialog.tsx` — remove useInputLayer, rely on when predicates
- `apps/km-tui/src/views/ProjectPicker.tsx` — same
- `apps/km-tui/src/views/NewItemDialog.tsx` — same
- `apps/km-tui/src/tui.tsx` — remove InputLayerProvider wrapper

## Dependencies
- Requires L2 (createApp + Zustand store) first

title: km view: lazy loading for very large drives
description:
Point km view at any drive without choking. Faster startup for large directories.

## Design: preloadDepth + Background Indexing

**preloadDepth** (default: Infinity — current behavior, zero breaking changes):
- Walk to preloadDepth eagerly at startup. Discover files, parse markdown, resolve links.
- This is what renders immediately.

**Background phase** (when preloadDepth < Infinity):
- After initial render, continue loading remaining directories in background during idle time.
- Links resolve progressively — unresolved refs "light up" as their targets load.
- Search works on loaded content, gets progressively more complete.
- Once background completes, full search and all links resolved.

## Architecture Changes

1. **Storage (discovery.ts)**: Add preloadDepth to DiscoveryOptions. scanDirectory() tracks current depth. Beyond preloadDepth, directories are marked "unexplored" with a shallow readdir count (no stat). New expandDirectory(path, db) function discovers a single directory subtree incrementally.

2. **Storage (repo.ts)**: Add preloadDepth to CreateRepoOptions. Repo exposes expandDirectory() for on-demand expansion + getUnexploredDirs() for background loader. Repo exposes backgroundLoadRemaining() that progressively expands all unexplored dirs.

3. **TUI**: Unexplored directories show dimmed "~N items" indicator. Expanding triggers expandDirectory() + re-render. Background loader calls backgroundLoadRemaining() after first render.

4. **Search**: Searches whatever is in the db. Partial during background loading, complete after. No special handling needed — SQLite FTS just works on available data.

## Key: No Breaking Changes
- preloadDepth defaults to Infinity = current behavior
- All existing code paths unchanged
- Feature is opt-in via config or CLI flag
notes: User confirmed hybrid approach: eager to maxDepth + lazy beyond. Unresolved cross-depth refs are acceptable — they light up as you navigate. Primary goals: any drive without choking + faster startup.
close_reason: Implemented preloadDepth in storage layer. Default Infinity (no behavior change). When finite: directory walk stops at depth limit, records unexplored dirs with readdir child counts. Repo exposes expandDirectory() for on-demand expansion and expandAll() async generator for background indexing. 10 tests in preload-depth.test.ts. All 4221 tests pass.

title: Remove manual dimension calculations — use inkx/flexx layout
description:
## Goal
Remove manual dimension calculations across km-tui in favor of automatic inkx/flexx layout. When inkx/flexx lacks needed features, fix them directly.

## Anti-Patterns to Eliminate

### A: Manual inner width/height calculation
```tsx
// BAD: manually subtracting border/padding
const innerWidth = Math.max(10, width - 6)
<Box width={innerWidth}>...</Box>

// GOOD: let flex layout handle it
<Box>...</Box>  // children auto-fill parent content area
```

### B: Manual text truncation
```tsx
// BAD: .slice() for truncation
const text = content.slice(0, width - 3)

// GOOD: inkx wrap=truncate
<Text wrap="truncate">{content}</Text>
```

### C: Manual centering with padding
```tsx
// BAD: compute padding to center text
const leftPad = Math.floor((width - text.length) / 2)
{' '.repeat(leftPad)}{text}{' '.repeat(rightPad)}

// GOOD: flex centering
<Box justifyContent="center"><Text>{text}</Text></Box>
```

### D: Manual separator/border drawing
```tsx
// BAD: repeat chars for HR
{'─'.repeat(innerWidth - 2)}

// GOOD: Box with borderBottom or dedicated <HR/> component
<Box borderBottom="single" />
```

### E: Manual Math.max guards
```tsx
// BAD: defensive guard against negative
Math.max(0, width - 2)
Math.max(10, width - 6)

// GOOD: inkx handles small/zero dimensions
<Box overflow="hidden">...</Box>
```

### F: width={N} on children inside flex parents
```tsx
// BAD: explicit width on flex children
<Box width={width}><Box width={innerWidth}>...</Box></Box>

// GOOD: flexGrow or omit width
<Box width={width}><Box flexGrow={1}>...</Box></Box>
```

### G: Manual height reserves for fixed elements
```tsx
// BAD: subtract header/footer heights
height={height - 3}

// GOOD: use flexGrow on the flexible area
<Box flexDirection="column" height={height}>
  <Box height={1} flexShrink={0}>header</Box>
  <Box flexGrow={1}>content</Box>
  <Box height={1} flexShrink={0}>footer</Box>
</Box>
```

### H: Manual column count calculation
```tsx
// MAY BE LEGITIMATE if inkx lacks auto-grid
Math.floor((width - 1) / (colWidth + 1))
// But check if inkx has flexWrap or similar
```

## Search Keywords
```
width - [0-9]   height - [0-9]   innerWidth   innerHeight
Math.max(       Math.min(        Math.floor(  Math.ceil(
.repeat(        .slice(0,        .padEnd(     .padStart(
width={         height={         width=\`
```

## Files with Manual Calcs
DetailPane.tsx, CardColumn.tsx, Board.tsx, ColumnsView.tsx, ListView.tsx, TabsView.tsx, HelpOverlay.tsx, FilterDialog.tsx, ConsoleModal.tsx, OverflowIndicator.tsx, render.ts, layout/path.ts
notes:
Audit found manual calcs in: DetailPane.tsx (innerWidth, separator repeat, maxEntries), CardColumn.tsx (width-1, width-2, height-2, separator repeat), ColumnsView.tsx (height-2, height-1), ListView.tsx (height-1), TabsView.tsx (height-3), HelpOverlay.tsx (centering math), FilterDialog.tsx (innerWidth), ConsoleModal.tsx (height calc), OverflowIndicator.tsx (manual centering), Board.tsx (colCount, cardsPerCol), render.ts (slice for truncation, colWidth), layout/path.ts (truncation). Categories: (A) Flex replacements: innerWidth, width-N on children. (B) Separator/border: repeat() for HR lines. (C) Text centering: manual padding. (D) Text truncation: .slice() instead of wrap=truncate. (E) Legitimate layout math: column counting, virtualization heights.
Also update .claude/skills/code/clean.md with Layout Anti-Patterns section when implementing.

title: Markdown prefix conversion: type '- ', '# ', '1. ', '[] ' to convert node type; backspace to strip
description:
Roam/Notion-style markdown prefix conversion during inline editing. Two behaviors:

## 1. Prefix Conversion (typing)

When the user types a recognized markdown prefix at the START of a node's content in edit mode, convert the node type and strip the prefix from content:

| Prefix typed | Resulting type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `- ` | li (bulleted) | Unordered list item, marker='-' |
| `* ` | li (bulleted) | Unordered list item, marker='*' |
| `1. ` | li (numbered) | Ordered list item |
| `# ` | oi (section) | h1 depth heading/section |
| `## ` | oi (section) | h2 depth |
| `### ` | oi (section) | h3 depth |
| `[] ` or `[ ] ` | task trait | Add task_marker '[ ]', keep type |
| `[x] ` | task trait | Add task_marker '[x]' (done) |
| `> ` | quote | Block quote |
| `--- ` or `*** ` or `___ ` | hr | Horizontal rule (integrates with km-tui.hr-edit) |
| `\`\`\` ` | code | Code block (fenced) |

Detection: trigger when user types the space (or newline for code fence) after the prefix. Strip the prefix from displayed content.

### HR Integration

The `---` prefix conversion integrates with km-tui.hr-edit: typing '---' + space converts the node to type=hr with content='---'. The HR edit spec handles subsequent editing, display (centered), and type reversion (backspace strips hr back to p).

## 2. Backspace Stripping (at beginning of line)

When user presses backspace at position 0 (beginning of content), strip features in priority order BEFORE merging with previous node:

1. **First**: If node has task trait → remove task_marker (keep type)
2. **Then**: If node type is non-paragraph (li, h, hr, quote, code, etc.) → convert to p
3. **Finally**: If already a plain p with no traits → merge with previous node (existing behavior)

This creates a progressive 'undo' of the node's special formatting before destructive merge.

## Node Types Reference (km-core)

Block types: p, h, code, quote, table, hr, html, math
Item types: oi (outline item), li (list item)
Link type: link

Not all types make sense for prefix conversion (table, html, math are complex structures). The prefixes above cover the common markdown shortcuts.

## Reference

Inspired by Decker's block editing model and Roam/Notion's markdown shortcuts.

title: Multi-select operations: batch delete, status toggle
description:
Extend batch operation support to remaining single-node-only operations:

## Operations to add

title: My Tasks board is flat — missing section grouping from Asana
description: The 'My Tasks' view for users shows a flat list of tasks without section grouping. In Asana, My Tasks has sections (e.g., Recently Assigned, Today, Upcoming) that group tasks. The km import doesn't preserve this section structure, or the board view doesn't render it. Tasks should be grouped by their section within the My Tasks project.
notes:
## Investigation Findings

### Root Cause
Asana API does NOT include user_task_list sections in the memberships field. Orphan tasks (only in My Tasks) have empty memberships. The existing code tried to derive sections from memberships using user_task_list GID as project GID — always returned empty.

### Solution
Use the assignee_section field on tasks (contains My Tasks section GID/name like 'Recently assigned', 'Do today', 'Do later').

### Changes
1. asana-types.ts: Added assignee_section.name to TASK_FIELDS and AsanaApiTask interface
2. asana-api.ts: Added deriveAssigneeSections(), getTaskSectionGid(), useAssigneeSection flag. User task list imports now use assignee_section
3. fake-asana.ts: Updated test fixture with assignee_section data
4. import.test.ts: Added section grouping assertions for user task lists

### Limitation
assignee_section is only returned for the authenticated user's own tasks.

### Status
Fix implemented, all 77 import tests passing.
Fix implemented: Use assignee_section field from Asana API for user task lists instead of memberships. Files: asana-types.ts (added field), asana-api.ts (deriveAssigneeSections + useAssigneeSection flag). Tests pass. Re-import required to pick up changes.

title: Unified navigateToNode() replacing findZoomTarget + inline zoom logic
description: O3 recommendation: Extract a single navigateToNode(target, repo) function that replaces both findZoomTarget() and the inline logic in handleSearchSelect(). Structure-aware ancestor walking: walk up the chain, stop at the lowest ancestor that yields a multi-column layout (>=2 oi children). Returns { action: SELECT|ZOOM_IN|DETAIL_VIEW, zoomTarget?, cursorTarget? }. Reusable for search, deep links, breadcrumb navigation, any 'go to' feature. Replaces both findZoomTarget() and inline logic in handleSearchSelect().

title: Replace noColor with <StripColor> wrapper component
description:
Replace noColor threading with a `<StripColor>` wrapper component (or inkx Box prop `stripColor`).

Current: 15+ components check `ctx.noColor ? undefined : "\$token"`.

Better: Components ALWAYS set their natural color (`color="\$link"`, `color="\$control"`). When the parent card is selected/highlighted, wrap content in `<StripColor>` — this neutralizes all descendant color props so everything uses the inherited fg (e.g. \$selectedfg).

```tsx
// Selected card:
<Box backgroundColor="\$selected" color="\$selectedfg">
  <StripColor>
    <InlineText text={content} />   {/* links, code, sigils all render as \$selectedfg */}
  </StripColor>
</Box>

// Normal card:
<Box>
  <InlineText text={content} />     {/* links=\$link, code=\$control, etc. */}
</Box>
```

Implementation options:
1. **React context**: StripColor sets a context flag, useTheme/resolveThemeColor returns undefined for all tokens when flag is set
2. **inkx Box prop**: `stripColor` on Box tells the renderer to ignore descendant color props
3. **Transform**: A Transform-like component that strips ANSI color codes from rendered output

Option 1 is simplest — just a context provider that short-circuits theme color resolution.

title: Cards: OSC 8 escape garbage in body content from links
description: Card body content shows raw OSC 8 escape sequences from hyperlinks instead of clean text. The pretty-URL feature adds OSC 8 hyperlinks but card body truncation/display doesn't handle them properly.

Each pane is a self-contained view into the repo. The workspace manages N panes, each with its own state. No hardcoded one-or-two pane assumption.

### Phase 6: Discriminated union pane types

workspace: { panes: Map<string, PaneState>, focusedPaneId, layout }

design:
## Vision

Each pane is a self-contained view into the repo. The workspace manages N panes, each with its own state. No hardcoded one-or-two pane assumption.

## Current Architecture (problems)

- `BoardAppState` has flat fields (rootId, cursorNodeId, foldDepths, etc.) that represent the "active" pane
- `UIState` has per-pane state stranded as global fields (collapsedColumns, multiSelected, visualMode, inlineEditBlock, localSearch, etc.)
- `PaneState` exists but is a secondary mirror — snapshot/restore dance on focus switch
- Detail pane is special-cased (showDetailPane, detailCursorNodeId, CursorAwareDetailPane)
- Adding a new pane type requires hardcoded logic

## Target Architecture

```
workspace: {
  panes: Map<string, PaneState>    // THE source of truth
  focusedPaneId: string
  layout: LayoutNode
}
```

### BoardPaneState (can have several)

Per-board-view state — navigation, cursor, selection, folds, view mode. Multiple board panes can coexist (e.g., side-by-side boards, or a board + detail).

```
BoardPaneState {
  id, viewType: "board"
  rootId, cursorNodeId, selectedNodes, foldDepths, collapsedNodes,
  viewMode, collapsedColumns, columnScrollAnchor,
  multiSelected, selectionAnchor, visualMode,
  inlineEditBlock, localSearch, searchReplace,
  showIgnored, moveMode, moveSourceNodes, ...
}
```

### DetailPaneState

```
DetailPaneState {
  id, viewType: "detail"
  rootNodeId       // which node is displayed (slaved to a board pane's cursor)
  cursorId         // topbar / meta row / child — navigation within detail
  scrollOffset
  slavedTo: string // pane ID of the board it follows
}
```

### PaneState = BoardPaneState | DetailPaneState | ...

Discriminated union on viewType. Future: console, sync, search results, etc.

### AppState (truly global)

```
AppState {
  workspace: WorkspaceState
  ui: UIState  // dimensions, iconStyle, clipboard, dialogs, bell, status, pendingChord
  repo, repoPath, ...
}
```

Flat fields (rootId, cursorNodeId, etc.) eliminated. Actions read/write through panes.get(focusedPaneId). The snapshot/restore dance goes away.

## Pane Relationships

- Detail pane is "slaved" to a board pane: follows board cursor when board is focused, freezes when detail is focused
- This is a relationship property, not special-cased logic
- slavedTo field on DetailPaneState identifies the master pane

## Migration Strategy

Incremental — cannot do this in one pass:
1. Move detail pane root node into PaneState (immediate — unblocks detail focus work)
2. Move per-pane UIState fields into BoardPaneState
3. Make actions read/write through panes map instead of flat fields
4. Eliminate flat fields and snapshot/restore dance
5. Add discriminated union for different pane types

## Design Questions

- Should actions dispatch to the focused pane, or should the pane ID be explicit in every action?
- How do "slave" pane updates work — eager cross-pane writes, or derive-on-read?
- Does each pane get its own CursorStore, or is cursor state folded into PaneState directly?
- How does this interact with TEA state machines — is each pane its own state machine?
notes:
Reclassified from review:
- rootBoardId: per-pane (it IS the pane's root node for sigil exclusion — same as PaneState.rootId)
- maxContentLines: per-pane (different panes, different density)
- showDetailPane: eliminated (derived from layout containing a viewType=detail pane)
Phase 3 complete (23a29035): eliminated 13 flat board fields from BoardAppState. workspace.panes is now canonical. getActiveBoardPane() exported as the single accessor pattern. 23 test files migrated. All 199 fast test files pass (4253 tests). Remaining phases: Phase 2 (move per-pane UIState fields to BoardPaneState — selection, column, edit, search, filter, view, mouse, navHistory).
2026-03-01: Phase 2 complete (291eee9d). Moved 21 per-pane UIState fields to BoardPaneState via PerPaneUIFields interface. Smart routing setUI(), usePaneUI() hook, createInitialPaneUI() factory. Renamed EffectiveUIState→PaneUI, useEffectiveUI→usePaneUI. 37 files, 4253 tests passing. Phases 1-3 all committed.

title: TUI architecture refactor: unified state, sync layout, fine-grained updates
description:
# Architecture Refactor: Cursor Movement < 5ms

## Goal
Cursor movement (j/k/h/l) must feel instant on a 1440-node board. Target: <5ms per keypress.

## Benchmark (2026-02-08, 1440 nodes, 200x60)
| Action | before | after phase 1 |
|--------|--------|---------------|
| cards j | 86ms | 73ms |
| list j | 46ms | 33ms |
| columns j | 40ms | 25ms |
| h/l | 93ms | 73ms |

## Phase 1 — COMPLETED
TreeRenderContext, flat Zustand store, reduced subscriptions. Commits: f8d46c51, 7463ae9c, e556e2da, ffebb213.

## Phase 2 — New architecture

### Primitives

**Per-node children cache** in repo. Lazy (populated on demand), surgical invalidation (addNode→bust parent, moveNode→bust old+new, updateNode→nothing, deleteNode→bust parent). All consumers benefit: rendering, navigation, path derivation.

**Path** (number[]). SlateJS-aligned structural coordinate system. Derived lazily from cursorNodeId via cache lookups (no SQL). Pure arithmetic helpers: parent, next, previous, compare, isAncestor.

**ViewNavigation**. One rule: move to the next selectable node in that direction. Cards are the only wrapping container — h/l from inside a card hits the card boundary. All cross-group lateral movement uses curswantY.

### Store (minimal)
```
cursorNodeId: string
rootId: string | null
foldedNodes: Set<string>
selectedNodes: Set<string>
viewMode: ViewMode
```

### Key input flow
```
keypress
  → view.navigate(dir, cursorNodeId, curswantY)
    → uses repo.getChildren (cached) to find next selectable node
  → store.set({ cursorNodeId: newId })
```

### Render flow
```
cursorNodeId changed → Zustand notifies
  → Board re-renders
    → useChildren(repo, rootId) — from cache
    → each Column: useChildren(repo, colId) — from cache
    → each Card: useChildren(repo, cardId) — from cache
    → isSelected via store selector (per component)
    → React.memo: only old + new cursor nodes re-render
  → inkx render pipeline
```

### Mutation flow
```
action → repo.mutate(...)
  → cache: surgical invalidation (affected parents only)
  → store.set({ cursorNodeId: targetId })
  → Zustand notifies → re-render
    → useChildren: cache miss for affected parents only, hits for rest
```

### What gets removed
ColumnsLayout, ColumnState, CardState, colIndex, cardIndex, subPath, subIndex, selectionLevel, isAtCardLevel, isInOutlineMode, COLUMN_HEADER_INDEX, recomputeLayout, deriveCursorPosition, deriveColumnsFromRepo, useColumns, useCursorPosition, updateLayout effect, store→React→store feedback loop, status bar position display, columnIndex/siblingIndex in command context.

### Implementation steps
1. Per-node children cache in repo
2. NodePath module (pathOf, nodeAt, siblings)
3. useChildren(repo, parentId) hook
4. ViewNavigation per view
5. Remove old layout system
6. Profile render pipeline
7. Targeted per-node signals if profiling shows selector cost matters

### Acceptance criteria
1. j/k/h/l < 5ms on 1440-node board, zoom < 20ms
2. No pre-computed layout indices — all derived lazily via Path + cache
3. No store→React→store feedback loop
4. One navigation rule, view-resolved
5. Documented in docs/design/visual-navigation.md
notes:
## Phase 3 Results (2026-02-08)
- cards_j: 76ms → 19ms (bench), ~13ms (isolated)
- content phase: 12ms → 3.4ms (scroll container optimization)
- layout phase: 3.4ms (top bar text changes → full Flexx recalc)
- VirtualList: no re-render when cursor within visible window
- Remaining bottleneck: layout recalculation on every j/k (top bar path text)
- h/l: 64ms (column change still expensive — full board re-render)
- zoom: 101ms (full re-layout expected)

title: Prevent Column re-render on within-column cursor movement
description:
# Prevent Column re-render on within-column cursor movement

## Problem
When j/k moves cursor between cards within the same column, Column re-renders because
`useIsCursorInColumn(colIndex)` returns a new object whenever `cardIndex` changes.
This cascades: Column → VirtualList → ~50 renderItem calls → ~50 Card memo comparisons.

Only 2 Cards actually differ (old/new cursor), costing ~3ms. The other ~20ms is wasted
on Column + VirtualList re-renders.

## Current: 24ms for j/k
- Column re-render (~8-12ms): useIsCursorInColumn returns new object
- VirtualList renderItem loop (~8-10ms): 50 renderItem calls
- 2 Card re-renders (~2-3ms): actual work
- Ink toTerminal (~2-3ms): buffer diff

## Target: <5ms for j/k (common case)

## Solution
1. Split `useIsCursorInColumn` into:
   - `useIsColumnSelected(colIndex)` → { isSelected, selectionLevel } — stable on j/k
   - `useCursorCardIndex(colIndex)` → number — for scroll tracking only

2. Column subscribes to `useIsColumnSelected` only — doesn't re-render on j/k

3. Add `ColumnScrollTracker` (null-rendering component) that:
   - Subscribes to `useCursorCardIndex`
   - Calls `virtualListRef.scrollToItem()` imperatively
   - Only causes VirtualList re-render when scroll offset actually changes

4. Card uses `useIsCursorAtCard` exclusively (remove prop dependency)

## Expected: Common case (cursor in window) = ~3ms
- Column: no re-render ✓
- VirtualList: no re-render (scroll offset unchanged) ✓
- 2 Cards: re-render via CursorStore (~3ms) ✓
notes:
## Progress (2026-02-08)
- Implemented Card CursorStore self-subscription (useIsCursorAtCard)
- Added useIsColumnSelected (stable on j/k), useCursorCardIndex (scroll tracking)
- Column still re-renders on j/k for VirtualList scrollTo prop
- Benchmark: 76ms → 40ms (cards_j avg)
- Imperative scroll approach gave 24ms but broke tests (act() flushing issue)
- Deep research request sent for 2nd opinion on achieving <5ms

title: Performance regression after Phase 6 store refactor + NodeLine unification
description:
## Performance Regression After Phase 6 Store Refactor

The TUI is noticeably slower after the Phase 6 store refactor (commits b4d68773..e41bab6b).
This replaced RTK/immer/reselect with a plain Zustand-like store + useSyncExternalStore.

## Root Causes (ranked by impact)

### P0 — useApp() hook missing equality check (SMOKING GUN)

The `useApp()` hook in `vendor/beorn-inkx/src/runtime/create-app.tsx:214` does NOT compare
old vs new selected values before calling setState:

```tsx
useEffect(() => {
  return store.subscribe((newState) => {
    setState(() => selectorRef.current(newState))  // ALWAYS fires — no Object.is check
  })
}, [store])
```

Compare with zustand's `useStore`:
```tsx
// zustand checks: if (Object.is(currentSlice, nextSlice)) return;
```

Board.tsx now has 7 separate useAppStore() calls (lines 521-537):
- s.ui, s.boardState, s.toastQueue, s.layoutRegistry, s.setUI, s.dispatchBoard, s.updateLayout

Every store mutation fires ALL 7 subscriptions, each calling setState unconditionally.
React batches within a single event but the diffing/reconciliation cost is multiplied.

With RTK/reselect, memoized selectors would return the same reference for unchanged slices.
Now, every store change = 7 setState calls = 7 potential re-renders of Board.

### P0 — updateLayout() write-back creates render loop

Board.tsx:631-644:
```tsx
useEffect(() => {
  updateLayout(columnsLayout, selectedNode, derivedSelectionLevel, tuiBoardState)
}, [columnsLayout, selectedNode, derivedSelectionLevel, tuiBoardState, updateLayout])
```

This writes derived state BACK into the store after every render.
updateLayout calls set({layout, selectedNode, selectionLevel, tuiBoardState}),
which fires all subscribers again, potentially causing a second render cycle per keypress.

### P1 — assembleBoardState() creates new objects on every dispatch

board-app-store.ts:115-143: Every dispatchBoard call goes through withBoardState(),
which spreads `{...state, ...flatUpdate}` then calls assembleBoardState(),
creating a brand new boardState object even when only unrelated fields changed.
Board reads `s.boardState` — always gets a new ref → always re-renders.

### P1 — tuiBoardState useMemo has unstable deps

Board.tsx:609-623: `tuiBoardState` depends on `[boardState, columnsLayout]`.
Since boardState is a new object every dispatch (P1 above), this useMemo
NEVER memoizes — it recomputes every render, creating a new TUIBoardState.
This cascades through the entire component tree.

### P1 — N×useAppStore subscriptions in TreeNode

TreeNode.tsx:170-172: Every TreeNode instance subscribes to the store:
```tsx
const isFolded = useAppStore<BoardAppStore, boolean>(s => s.foldedNodes.has(node.id))
```

For a board with 200 cards, that's 200+ store subscriptions, each running their
selector on every store change. Without equality checks in useApp(), each fires setState.

### P2 — useBoardDialogs returns new handler object every render

use-board-dialogs.ts: Returns a plain object `{handleProjectSelect, handleProjectCancel, ...}`.
The individual handlers use useCallback, but the containing object is new every render.
BoardCore receives this as `dialogHandlers` prop — new ref every time.

### P2 — NodeLine renders renderRich() inline without memoization

shared-components.tsx:441: `{renderRich(title)}` is called on every render.
renderRich parses markdown + applies styles — non-trivial for 200+ visible nodes.
No React.memo on NodeLine means parent re-renders cascade.

### P3 — countVisibleDescendants is O(n) recursive and unused?

Board.tsx:785-807: This function exists but may not be called in the hot path.
If called during render, it walks the tree recursively for each visible card.

### P3 — new Set<string>() in tuiBoardState factory

Board.tsx:614: `selectedCards: new Set<string>()` creates a new Set every render.
While cheap, it means shallow comparison always fails for this field.

## Fix Plan (priority order)

1. **Fix useApp() equality check** — Add Object.is comparison in the subscriber:
   ```tsx
   store.subscribe((newState) => {
     const next = selectorRef.current(newState)
     setState(prev => Object.is(prev, next) ? prev : next)
   })
   ```

2. **Stabilize boardState ref** — Only create new boardState when flat fields actually change.
   Compare before/after in withBoardState.

3. **Remove or debounce updateLayout write-back** — Use a ref instead of store for layout,
   or gate the write with shallow equality check.

4. **Memoize useBoardDialogs return** — Wrap in useMemo.

5. **Add React.memo to NodeLine** — Trivial win for list rendering.

6. **Consider single useAppStore call** — Read all needed values in one selector to reduce
   subscription count from 7 to 1.
notes: 2026-02-07: Additional fix — updateLayout now uses silent mutation (bypasses Zustand set()) to eliminate double doRender() per keypress. Also added hit-count bell rate limiting for boundary auto-repeat (bellHitCount ≤ 2 fires, 3+ suppressed). Commit 37124478.

title: Performance review: board open and zoom-in latency
description: Profile and fix board opening and zoom-in latency. Prior analysis showed ~1.9s React reconciliation + 292ms inkx pipeline on initial mount. User reports it's still not fast enough.
notes:
Finding 1 (FIXED): useColumnReveal reset on every foldDepths change, not just zoom. Caused progressive reveal (skeleton columns) on every fold/unfold. Fix: only reset on rootId change.

Finding 2 (FIXED): useColumns re-derived all columns on foldDepths change even though kNodeToColumnView ignores foldDepths (param is _foldDepths). Fix: removed foldDepths from effect dependency tracking — fold state flows through Jotai atoms to TreeNode, not through column structure.

Key insight from user: root operations (loading, zoom) should complete all state computation synchronously in the store, then hand fully-computed state to React for rendering. Progressive RENDERING (stagger column mount) is fine for zoom. But don't confuse it with progressive LOADING — the loading path accidentally triggered on in-place operations (fold, select) that should be instant.

title: H/L progressive fold/unfold — reveal more depth levels
description: H/L fold/unfold is currently binary (folded or not). User expects progressive behavior: pressing L multiple times reveals deeper levels of the tree (grandchildren, great-grandchildren), pressing H multiple times collapses deeper levels first. Current impl: FOLD_NODE adds card.id to foldedNodes set, UNFOLD_NODE removes it. No per-card depth tracking. Need: per-card outline depth that L increments and H decrements.
notes:
CORRECTION: Decker fold depth is CALCULATED, not stored.

Decker model:
- Each node has a boolean 'folded' property (like km's foldedNodes set)
- getFoldLevel(ed, at) COMPUTES min/max/curr depth by scanning which nesting levels are folded
- foldTreeMore(): finds shallowest unfolded depth in subtree → folds all nodes at that depth
- unfoldTreeMore(): finds deepest folded depth in subtree → unfolds all nodes at that depth
- Net effect: progressive fold/unfold without storing any depth number

km approach should match:
- Keep foldedNodes: Set<string> as-is
- H (fold_node): scan children of cursor card, find deepest visible level, fold all nodes at that level
- L (unfold_node): scan children of cursor card, find shallowest folded level, unfold all nodes at that level
- Progressive behavior emerges from the scan, no new state needed

title: PTY integration tests: close the headless-vs-production testing gap
description:
## Problem: Headless Tests Pass, Production Breaks

Across 12+ sessions (2026-02-06 through 2026-02-08), headless tests consistently passed while the real TUI had visible bugs (visual bell flashes, cursor freezing on auto-repeat). Root cause: headless tests bypass the real async event pipeline:
- Headless: `board.press("j")` → `parseKey()` → `handleKey()` → synchronous
- Production: stdin → TermProvider → splitRawInput → event queue → processEventBatch → render

The key differences:
1. **No event batching**: headless tests process one key at a time, production batches auto-repeat bursts
2. **No timing**: headless tests are instantaneous, production has real latency between events and renders
3. **No terminal rendering**: headless tests check DOM/virtual buffer, production goes through the full ansi-diff → stdout pipeline

## Current State (partially fixed)

Created `apps/km-tui/tests/pty-integration.slow.spec.ts` using `createTtyEngine` (Bun PTY + @xterm/headless). This runs the REAL app in a REAL terminal pipeline (same stdin→terminal flow as production). 7 tests at 400x150:
- Startup, single j, burst j×10, rapid individual presses, large burst j×30, arrow keys, mixed keys

Also have TTY MCP tools (`mcp__tty__start`, `mcp__tty__screenshot`, etc.) for interactive visual verification.

## What's Still Missing

1. **PTY tests are slow** (~20-30s each due to startup + settle waits). Need faster warm-start or session reuse.
2. **No visual regression testing**: PTY tests check text content but not pixel-level rendering. Can't detect:
   - White flash artifacts
   - Cursor position rendering bugs
   - Color/style regressions
3. **No auto-repeat simulation**: `engine.press("j")` sends one key event. Real auto-repeat sends keys at 30Hz with specific timing. Need `engine.repeatKey("j", { count: 20, rateHz: 30 })`.
4. **No screenshot comparison**: `mcp__tty__screenshot` captures what we'd see, but no automated comparison between expected and actual.
5. **CI integration**: PTY tests need `*.slow.spec.ts` pattern to separate from fast tests.

## Proposed Approach

1. Add `engine.repeatKey()` to `tty-engine` that simulates real auto-repeat timing
2. Add screenshot capture to PTY tests (use `bufferToHTML()` from engine)
3. Create visual regression baseline snapshots
4. Speed up PTY tests: keep engine running across tests, use fresh vault per test
5. Integrate into `bun run test:slow` CI step

title: Investigate reactive state management for repo→UI data flow
description:
## Problem

`repo.version` (auto-incrementing counter on mutations) is used in `useMemo` deps to invalidate UI caches. Issues:

1. **Fragile accounting**: Every mutation method must remember `version++` — miss one and UI goes stale silently
2. **Dead read**: `useMemo` deps only checked on re-render — relies on co-occurring UI dispatch
3. **Full recompute**: Any mutation recomputes entire `useColumns` derivation (all columns + all cards)
4. **Getter/setter needed**: `versionHolder` pattern exists because mutation methods are created before `repo` object — structurally necessary, not accidental

## Current architecture

```
mutation → version++ → hope React re-renders → useMemo checks version → re-derive all columns
```

useColumns reads repo.getChildren(rootId) + getChildren(columnId) for each column. Pure derivation, but creates fresh objects every time (breaks React.memo referential equality).

## Analysis of approaches

### Quick fix: SQLite total_changes()
Replace manual `version++` with `db.prepare("SELECT total_changes()").pluck().get()`. SQLite maintains this counter automatically — eliminates accounting risk. Same dead-read limitation.

### useSyncExternalStore (medium)
Add subscribe/getSnapshot to Repo. afterMutation hook notifies subscribers → React re-renders automatically. Eliminates dead-read problem. Still recomputes everything.

### Normalized reactive store (full solution)
Maintain a normalized store (Map<id, Node> + Map<parentId, childId[]>) alongside SQLite. Components subscribe to their slice via selectors. Only affected components re-render. This is what Decker does with Slate between Yjs and React.

## Reference: How others solve this

### Slate (rich text editor)
- Editor is mutable singleton (like our repo)
- `onChange` callback registered via WeakMap, fires on every operation
- Callback increments version `v` in React context → subscribers re-render
- Hooks: `useSlate()` (all changes), `useSlateSelection()` (selection only) — granular subscriptions
- Source: https://github.com/ianstormtaylor/slate/blob/main/packages/slate-react/src/components/slate.tsx

### Decker (boardliner)
- Zustand for UI state (selectedIds, draggingIds, editMode)
- Content lives in Yjs+Slate, NOT in Zustand
- Slate-Yjs bindings make Slate reactive to Yjs changes
- Per-component subscriptions via Zustand selectors
- Source: ~/Code/DZ/decker/apps/webapp/packages/decker-boardliner/src/store/

### SQLite reactivity landscape
- **Level 1 — Table-level invalidation**: Track which tables a query touches, re-run on any change. Simple, fast enough. Used by vlcn.io, ElectricSQL, observable-sqlite.
- **Level 2 — Differential dataflow**: Incremental computation pipelines, only process deltas.
- **Level 3 — Inverted index**: Index queries instead of data, pinpoint invalidation.
- Bun doesn't expose SQLite update_hook yet (https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/issues/4175)
- Since we're the only writer/reader, we don't need SQLite hooks — our afterMutation hook already knows when writes happen.
- References:
  - https://vlcn.io/blog/the-march-to-reactivity
  - https://riffle.systems/essays/prelude/
  - https://github.com/jorroll/observable-sqlite

## Key insight

Inline editing (useLineEdit) is local state — keystrokes don't touch repo. Repo mutations only happen on discrete actions (toggle status, move, delete, confirm edit). So full recompute frequency = discrete action frequency, not keystroke frequency. This may be fine for current scale.

## Recommendation

Start with useSyncExternalStore + total_changes() (eliminates accounting + dead reads). If profiling shows full recompute is too slow, upgrade to normalized store with per-component selectors.

title: Document recurrence design, cross-system research, and Asana import mapping
description:
Create comprehensive recurrence documentation:
1. docs/design/recurrence.md — km's recurrence model, cross-system comparison, completion-based vs fixed-schedule
2. Update Asana README with recurrence field mapping and encoding details
3. Add recurrence field to TASK_FIELDS + AsanaApiTask interface
4. Update ImportItem to support recurrence data from sources
5. Document how Asana encodes recurrence (undocumented API field)
notes:
## Completed Work

1. Created `docs/design/recurrence.md` — comprehensive recurrence design doc:
   - km data model (recurrence + recur_prev, clone-on-complete)
   - RRULE format reference with natural language mapping
   - Completion-based recurrence design (X-AFTER-COMPLETION extension)
   - Cross-system comparison table (Todoist, Obsidian, Asana, Things, OmniFocus, TickTick)
   - Full Asana → km RRULE mapping table
   - Implementation file index and TODO list

2. Updated `apps/km-cli/src/import/adapters/asana/README.md`:
   - Added recurrence to the field mapping table
   - Replaced "Not Mapped" recurrence entry with full Recurrence section
   - Documented Asana recurrence object format (all 5 types)
   - Added Asana → RRULE mapping table
   - Added undocumented fields section (recurrence is the only known one)
   - Added not-yet-fetched fields (completed_by, actual_time_minutes, liked, approval_status)

3. Updated `docs/ref/prior-art.md`:
   - Added Asana to clone-on-complete model users
   - Added section 5: Completion-Based Recurrence with cross-system comparison

4. Updated code:
   - Added `recurrence` to TASK_FIELDS in asana-types.ts
   - Added recurrence type to AsanaApiTask interface
   - Added `recurrence` field to ImportItem type
   - Added `asanaRecurrenceToRRule()` conversion function in task-transform.ts
   - Wired recurrence conversion into toImportItem()

## Research Findings

- Asana's `recurrence` field is NOT in the official OpenAPI spec
- Accessible via opt_fields=recurrence since ~Oct 2024 (community discovery)
- 5 types: daily, weekly, monthly, yearly, periodically (after completion)
- `periodically` = "repeat after completion" (max 30 days in Asana)
- iCal RRULE has NO standard for completion-based recurrence
- km uses X-AFTER-COMPLETION=1 custom RRULE parameter
- No other undocumented Asana fields found (checked full OpenAPI spec)

title: Unified task/block/item rendering and styling pipeline
description:
Unified NodeView component replacing 4+ separate rendering paths.

## API
```tsx
NodeView({ node, style, isSelected, width, height })
```

### Styles (detail levels)
| Style | Where | Content |
|---|---|---|
| board | Column header | title + child count |
| column | Section header (§) | section name + count |
| tab | Tab bar | title pill |
| line | Subitem in card/detail | icon + title (1 line, truncated) |
| card | Board column | icon + title + badges + N subitems (as lines) + overflow |
| detail | Side pane | metadata table + body + children (as cards) + backlinks |

### Cross-cutting props
- `isSelected` — cursor highlight (inverse/bold/border)
- Status-based styling — isDone/isDropped dims entire subtree; isWip/isBlocked get accent colors

### Key principle
Children recurse one level down: detail→card→line. Same rich text pipeline, same icon/color logic, same badge formatting at every level.

### Current duplication to eliminate
- TreeNode.tsx (card rendering)
- TaskDetailPane (detail rendering)
- FolderDetailPane (folder detail)
- ColumnItems (children in detail pane)
- tree-node-helpers.ts (style computation)
- detail-pane-helpers.ts (formatting)
- shared-components.tsx (card wrapper)

### Benefits
- 1 component, 1 code path for all node display
- Detail pane automatically gets bullet formatting, status icons
- Cards and detail pane always visually consistent
- Easier to add new styles (e.g., timeline, calendar cell)

title: Search dialog has input delay - keypresses eaten before dialog opens
description:
## Problem
When pressing `/` to open search, there's a noticeable delay before the dialog appears. Any keystrokes typed during this delay are lost/eaten, forcing users to wait before they can start typing their search query.

## Expected Behavior
Search dialog should open instantly (or near-instantly) so users can immediately start typing their search query in a fluid motion: `/china<Enter>` should work without pause.

## Actual Behavior
- Press `/`
- Delay of ~200-500ms before dialog appears
- Keypresses during delay are lost
- User must wait, then retype

## Impact
Breaks the fast keyboard-driven workflow. Users expect `/search<Enter>` to be a single fluid gesture.

## Potential Causes
1. React render cycle delay
2. Heavy `rawQuery(SELECT * FROM nodes)` on dialog mount
3. `useMemo` computation for initial results
4. Multiple re-renders during dialog setup

## Investigation
- Check if query can be deferred until after first render
- Consider showing dialog skeleton immediately, populate results async
- Profile render time with React DevTools

title: Selection model: abstract text selection and node selection into unified anchor/focus pattern
description:
Unify selection into a SlateJS-inspired anchor/focus model:

## Current State
- `selectionAnchor: { nodeId, sub }` + `multiSelected: Set<SelectionKey>` — redundant
- `multiSelected` is derived from anchor + cursor position in `updateSelectionRange`
- Text editing (inline edit) is separate from structural selection

## Target Model
```typescript
type Point = { nodeId: string; offset?: number }
type Selection = { anchor: Point; focus: Point } | null
```

- **anchor**: where selection started (fixed until new selection begins)
- **focus**: where cursor is now (moves with j/k/h/l navigation)
- **multiSelected**: computed/derived from walking tree between anchor and focus
- **offset**: optional, for text editing within a node (inline edit mode)

## Key Insights
- Like text editors: selection = range between two points, derived by walking the structure
- Like SlateJS: `Selection = { anchor: Point, focus: Point }`, operations (transforms) are separate
- Shift-j/k: focus moves vertically, selection = cards between anchor and focus
- Shift-h/l: focus moves to different column, selection = all cards in column range
- Normal navigation without shift: collapses selection (anchor = focus = cursor)
- Inline edit: same Point type with offset for character position

## References
- SlateJS Selection model: https://docs.slatejs.org/concepts/03-locations
- Decker removeNesting(): ensures flat selection at each tree depth level
design:
## Architecture: SlateJS-Inspired Anchor/Focus Selection

### Model
```typescript
type Point = { nodeId: string; offset?: number }  // offset for text cursor
type Selection = { anchor: Point; focus: Point } | null
// Collapsed: anchor === focus (single cursor)
// Node selection: offset undefined (whole node)
// Text selection: offset defined (character position)
```

### Prior Art
- **SlateJS**: `Range = { anchor: Point, focus: Point }` — single model for cursor, text range, and block selection. Helpers: `Range.isCollapsed()`, `Range.isBackward()`.
- **ProseMirror**: `TextSelection` vs `NodeSelection` — both are Selections with `anchor`/`head` positions
- **DOM Selection API**: `Selection = { anchorNode, anchorOffset, focusNode, focusOffset }`

### Key Decisions
1. **Single Selection object** replaces both `selectionAnchor` and `multiSelected: Set`
2. **offset=undefined** means whole-node selection; offset=number means text cursor
3. **Contiguous selection only** (no disjoint multi-select) — simplifies model dramatically
4. **Tree walk** to compute selected nodes between anchor and focus
5. **Selection stored in undo history** — each batch records `selectionBefore` for cursor restore
6. **Within-column constraint**: anchor and focus must share a parent (simplifies ordering)

### Implementation
1. Define `Point`, `Selection` types. Add helpers: `isCollapsed(sel)`, `isBackward(sel, tree)`, `nodesInRange(sel, tree)`
2. Replace `selectionAnchor` + `multiSelected` with single `selection: Selection | null` in store
3. `nodesInRange()`: walk tree from anchor.nodeId to focus.nodeId in document order, collect all nodes in between
4. Navigation: Shift+j/k moves focus only (anchor stays), expanding/shrinking range. Without Shift: collapse to `anchor = focus = newNode`
5. `isNodeSelected(nodeId)`: check if node falls between anchor and focus in tree order
6. Integrate with undo: store selection snapshot in each OperationBatch
7. Integrate with text-mode: when mode='text', selection has offset values; when mode='node', offset=undefined
8. Refactor all code using `multiSelected` to use `nodesInRange(selection, tree)` instead
notes: 2026-02-17: EditContext unification (km-tui.edit-context) provides the text cursor primitives this needs. EditContext's selectionStart/selectionEnd maps to the anchor/focus offset for text mode. Implement selection-abstraction AFTER edit-context lands — the unified cursor model simplifies the design.

title: Selection model: Esc clears, Shift-H/L selects columns, coherent tree-selection
description:
Three improvements to the multi-selection model:

## 1. Esc clears selection
Currently Esc routes to `close_or_quit` which cascades through overlays/modes but never checks `multiSelected`. There's a `clear_selection` command defined (selection.ts:70) mapped to Escape, but the keybinding (keybindings.ts:336) maps Escape to `close_or_quit` instead — making it unreachable.

**Fix**: Add selection clearing as a step in `handleCloseOrQuit()` cascade, before the final bell/boundary. If `multiSelected.size > 0`, clear it and return.

## 2. Shift-H/L selects columns
Currently Shift-H and Shift-L just clear selection (placeholder). They should select entire columns:
- Shift-L: select all cards in the column to the right (or extend column selection rightward)
- Shift-H: select all cards in the column to the left (or shrink/extend leftward)

## 3. Coherent tree-selection across depths (Decker model)
When selecting at different tree depths, the selection should normalize coherently:
- **Card-level** (Shift-J/K): individual card selection within a column (current behavior)
- **Column-level** (Shift-H/L): selects entire columns
- **Board-level** (Shift-A cycle): selects everything

Reference: Decker uses `removeNesting()` to ensure selection stays flat — no simultaneous parent-child selection. When you switch depths, selection normalizes to the new level. km should adopt a similar invariant: selecting at column level replaces card-level selections, and vice versa.

## Current state
- `ui.multiSelected: Set<SelectionKey>` tracks selected nodes
- `selectionAnchor` tracks range start for extend-select
- `selectAllLevel` cycles 0→1→2 (card→column→board)
- Shift-J/K work correctly for vertical card selection
- Shift-H/L are stubs that clear selection
- Esc doesn't check selection at all
design:
## Design: Anchor/Focus Selection Model

### Core Model
Selection is defined by two points: **anchor** (where shift-selection started) and **focus** (current cursor position). The visible selection is derived from these two points.

### State Changes
```typescript
// Current (positional):
selectionAnchor: { col: number; card: number; sub: number } | null

// Keep positional for now — nodeId-based is a follow-up refactor
```

### Selection Derivation Rules
- **Same column, same card**: sub-item range (outline mode)
- **Same column, different cards**: card range (Shift-J/K)
- **Different columns**: all cards in all columns from anchor to focus (Shift-H/L)

### Shift-H/L: Column Selection
`handleExtendSelectHorizontal` always produces column-level selection:
1. Set anchor at current position (if null)
2. Move cursor (focus) one column in direction
3. Select ALL cards in columns between anchor.col and focus.col
4. At boundary: if no selection yet, select current column only; if already have selection, do nothing

Uses its own column-range helper (not `updateSelectionRange`) because H/L always means 'entire columns', even when focus returns to anchor column.

### Escape: Clear Selection
Add to `handleCloseOrQuit` cascade, after overlays/modes but before nav-back:
```
if (ui.multiSelected.size > 0) { clearSelection(ctx); return ok() }
```

### Normal h/l with active selection
Already handled: `handleSelectionNav` in board-actions-nav.ts clears selection and falls through to normal horizontal navigation.

### Future: nodeId-based anchor/focus
Current positional indices are fragile if layout reflows mid-selection. Future refactor: `selectionAnchor: string | null` (nodeId), resolve to position via `layout.nodeIndex`. Not needed now since selections are transient.

### Future: Text vs Node selection abstraction
Both text selection (inline edit) and node selection (shift-movement) follow the anchor/focus pattern. Currently separate systems. Unification is future work — they operate in different modes and don't need to share state.

title: Selection model: convert anchor/focus from positional indices to nodeIds

Not urgent since selections are transient and layout doesn't change mid-selection.

description:
## Bug: Column shift (Meta+l/Meta+h) doesn't visually reorder columns

After Meta+l at a column header, the repo correctly swaps column sort orders, but the UI either doesn't re-render the new order or scrolls the target column off-screen.

### Root Causes (found on feat/virtual-columns branch)

**1. applyStructuralSharing missing reorder detection** (use-columns.ts)
- `applyStructuralSharing` compares prev/next column arrays for structural sharing
- When columns are swapped (Meta+l/Meta+h), their content doesn't change — only their ORDER
- The function checked `!anyColumnChanged && prev.length === next.length` and returned `prev` (old order)
- Missing: a loop comparing `prev[i].node.id !== next[i].node.id` to detect reordering
- Fix: Added order comparison loop before returning `prev`

**2. useVirtualization estimatedVisibleCount under-counts** (useVirtualization.ts)
- `Math.floor(viewportSize / (avgItemSize + gap))` rounds down aggressively
- With viewport=78, itemWidth=39, gap=1: floor(78/40)=1 but HVL renders 2 (boundary item included)
- Scroll algorithm thinks 1 visible → scrolls target column's neighbor off-screen after shift
- Fix: Changed to `Math.ceil` to match HVL's actual rendering behavior

**3. _layoutRepoVersion staleness check was removed** (board-app-store.ts)
- SELECT fast path didn't detect stale layout after repo mutation
- Fix: Restored the staleness check from main

### Test Verification
All 33 board-edit.spec tests pass after fixes.

title: Opt+h/l does not shift cards between columns in terminal
Shift down sends cards to bottom due to duplicate parent_idx
description:
When siblings have duplicate parent_idx values (e.g., all default to 0), the calculateSortOrder function computed fractional values between virtual sequential indices, but the actual DB sorts by real parent_idx. This caused the moved card to end up at the bottom of the column instead of the adjacent position.

Fix: Added normalizeSortOrders() that assigns sequential parent_idx [0,1,2,...] to column cards when duplicates are detected, called before any shift calculation in moveCardInColumn.

title: Per-item Slate editor: rich text + split/merge + undo/redo
description:
## Per-Item Slate Editor for km

Use `slate` core (not slate-react) as an **item-level** editing engine. Each card being edited gets a Slate editor instance — km keeps full control of tree structure and storage.

### Architecture

```
km tree (SQLite)                    Slate (per-item editor)
┌─────────────────┐                ┌──────────────────────┐
│ KNode {         │  ──hydrate──>  │ editor.children = [  │
│   content: md   │                │   { type: "paragraph",│
│   data: {...}   │                │     children: [Text] }│
│ }               │  <──serialize─ │ ]                     │
└─────────────────┘                └──────────────────────┘
```

**Slate owns**: content within one item (markdown inline formatting, paragraph split/merge, cursor/selection, undo/redo via slate-history)
**km owns**: tree between items (parent_id, parent_idx, move/reparent, indent/outdent)

### Why Slate Core

- **Path/Node interfaces**: tree addressing system
- **Transforms (apply())**: battle-tested split/merge/move with metadata+children handling
- **slate-history**: undo/redo per edit session for free
- **Normalization**: schema enforcement
- No DOM dependency in core `slate` package — runs in Node/Bun

### Enter Rules

| Cursor | Item State | Action | Type |
|---|---|---|---|
| Title, start | any | Insert empty sibling before | Tree op |
| Title, middle | title-only, no children | Split item into two siblings | Tree op |
| Title, middle | has body/children | Split: before stays, after+body+children→new sibling | Tree op |
| Title, end | title-only, no children | New empty sibling after | Tree op |
| Title, end | has body | Cursor moves into body | Cursor move |
| Title, end | children, no body | New empty first-child | Tree op |
| Body, start/mid | — | Split paragraph | Slate internal |
| Body, end (not last) | — | New paragraph after | Slate internal |
| Body, last, end | any | New body paragraph | Slate internal |

### Backspace Rules (at position 0)

| Cursor | Context | Action | Type |
|---|---|---|---|
| Title | empty, has prev | Delete, cursor to prev | Tree op |
| Title | empty, no prev, has parent | Delete, cursor to parent | Tree op |
| Title | content, prev childless | Merge prev content into this | Tree op |
| Title | content, prev has children | Move this as last child of prev | Tree op |
| Title | no prev, has parent | Outdent: sibling of parent | Tree op |
| Body, first para | — | Merge into title | Slate internal |
| Body, non-first | — | Merge with prev para | Slate internal |

### Hydration Layer

`markdown string ↔ Slate Element[]` using km's existing @km/markdown parser. On edit start: parse node content → Slate children. On save: serialize Slate children → markdown string → updateNode.

### Reference

See Decker (~/Code/DZ/decker/) withOutline.ts for Enter/Backspace patterns. km adapts these for per-item scope instead of whole-tree.

- initBoardStateGenerator completing (last progress message clears)
- React mounting and rendering the board

Likely causes in the gap:
1. createBoardAppStoreState setup (zustand store creation, undo system setup)
2. React first render (mounting all components, useColumns deriving, TreeNode recursion)
3. inkx layout computation (first frame layout for all visible cards)

Root cause: The CLI progress display likely overwrites previous lines (spinner behavior), so by the time alt screen activates, only the last line survives in scrollback.

title: Sync activity pane: toggleable panel showing per-file sync operations
description: Persistent, minimizable pane showing individual file sync events (synced, renamed, errors). Like Dropbox/OneDrive sync activity view. Requires: (1) per-file events from sync worker → TUI, (2) new SyncPane component, (3) keyboard toggle. Current infra only exposes aggregate WatcherStatus (state + counts) — no per-file data reaches the TUI yet.
design:
## Architecture: Event-Driven Subscriber + Toggleable Log Pane

### Model
- Sync worker emits fine-grained `SyncEvent { timestamp, filePath, eventType, details }` via IPC/EventEmitter
- Main thread subscribes and pushes to `syncEvents: SyncEvent[]` in Zustand (capped at ~100 entries)
- `<SyncPane>` component conditionally renders based on `showSyncPane` toggle

### Prior Art
- **Dropbox**: live list of files with statuses (syncing/paused/error)
- **VS Code Git panel**: updates per file change
- **rsync --progress**: per-file streaming output

### Key Decisions
1. **Push model** (event emitter) over polling — sync worker sends messages, UI subscribes
2. **Throttle rendering** at ~10 updates/sec if events are bursty (queue and batch)
3. **Fixed buffer** (~100 events) to cap memory
4. **Toggle via keybinding** (e.g. Alt-S) — pane takes bottom N lines when visible
5. **Minimized state**: when hidden, show one-line summary ("✓ Synced" or "⚠ 2 errors")

### Implementation
1. Extend sync worker to emit per-file events: `syncEmitter.emit('sync-event', { file, action, status })`
2. In main thread: `syncEmitter.on('sync-event', ev => store.addSyncEvent(ev))`
3. `addSyncEvent` Zustand action: prepend to array, trim if >100
4. `<SyncPane>` component: when visible, render scrollable list with color-coded status icons
5. Layout: reserve bottom 5-8 lines when pane is open, recalc main view height
6. When hidden: single status line in footer

**What should show**: Task titles (e.g., "Clean-up after trip", "Fix EPD", etc.)

But the TUI is rendering only the numeric GID, not the full title. Either:
1. The parser creates separate embed/link nodes that only carry the GID as content

3. The smart resolver isn't being called for these references

title: TUI test accuracy: unify testEnv/createApp + visual invariants
description:
Make TUI tests exercise the same rendering pipeline as production, and build visual invariant helpers that encode user vocabulary as assertions. Goal: user <=> AI TUI tests works ~100% of the time, eliminating dependency on GUI/TTY verification for bug closure.

Two work streams:
1. Unify testEnv/createApp rendering — testEnv has 5-iteration layout stabilization loop, production does single pass. This divergence caused 5/9 bugs in session 0215b to be prematurely closed.
2. Visual invariant system — every visual descriptor users use (borders missing, text truncated, blank area, ghost chars, alignment) becomes a composable assertion.

This is foundational technology that enables faster iteration loops.

title: Visual invariant assertion system
description: Build composable visual assertions that encode user vocabulary: expectBorderContinuous, expectTextTruncated, expectNoGhostChars, expectBlankRegion, expectIncrementalMatchesFresh, expectCursorVisible, etc. Every visual descriptor a user uses should have a corresponding test helper.
notes:
## Implementation Complete

### New assertions added to board-test.ts
1. **expectTextNotOverflowing(nodeId)** - Checks no non-space/non-border chars appear past node right edge. Catches text bleed into borders (km-silvery-legacy border text overflow bug).

2. **expectColumnsAligned(columnIds[])** - Verifies columns are:
   - Ordered left-to-right matching the provided ID array
   - Non-overlapping (each column left edge >= previous right edge)
   - Consistent height (±1px tolerance)

3. **expectTextTruncated(nodeId)** - Verifies that a node with long text has its rendered text shorter than the full DOM text content.

4. **expectNoContentGaps(contentRows?)** - Smarter blank-row detection that only checks rows within the content area (between first and last content rows), skipping legitimate spacers below content.

### Already existing (documented in skills/tests/tui.md)
- expectBorderContinuous, expectHorizontalBorder, expectAdjacentBorders
- expectNoGhostChars, expectBlankRegion, expectNoBlankLine
- expectCursorVisible, expectIncrementalMatchesFresh
- expectNodeColor, expectCellColor, expectCellChar, expectRow, expectScreen

### Tests
7 new tests in alignment.test.ts exercising the assertions. All 36 alignment tests pass.

### Docs updated
Updated .claude/skills/tests/tui.md buffer assertions table with complete list.

title: Unify testEnv and createApp rendering pipeline
description: testEnv uses a 5-iteration layout stabilization loop while production renders in a single pass. This means tests over-stabilize, masking bugs that appear in production. Additionally scroll state updates differ. Fix: make testEnv match production's single-pass behavior, or if production needs the loop, add it there too.
notes:
## Implementation Complete (All Tests Pass)

### What was done
1. Added `singlePassLayout` option to inkx test renderer (renderer.ts)
   - When true: doRender() runs up to 2 executeRender iterations (matching production processEventBatch pattern)
   - First executeRender triggers layout notifications -> forceUpdate -> hadReactCommit=true
   - Second executeRender picks up the layout feedback changes
   - sendInput() has a flush loop for layout feedback effects
   - Initial render always uses multi-pass for useContentRect stabilization

2. Added paintDirty=true to commitTextUpdate in host-config.ts (genuine fix: text content changes now correctly set paintDirty)

3. Added 8 passing tests in vendor/beorn-inkx/tests/single-pass-layout.test.tsx
4. Added 3 minimal repro tests in vendor/beorn-inkx/tests/single-pass-rerender.test.tsx

5. Enabled singlePassLayout=true in:
   - apps/km-tui/tests/helpers/board-test.ts (all 4 createRenderer calls)
   - apps/km-tui/src/driver.ts (createBoardDriver)

### Results
- All 117 inkx test files pass (2102+ tests, 0 failures)
- All 82 km-tui test files pass (1551 tests, 0 failures)
- Test renderer now matches production rendering pipeline

### Key insight
Production uses processEventBatch which can call doRender multiple times. The 2-pass solution in single-pass mode matches this: first pass renders, second pass picks up layout feedback. This is fundamentally different from the old 5-iteration stabilization loop which allowed unlimited re-renders.

title: Node mode / Text mode keybinding separation
description: Two distinct modes with separate keybinding sets. Node mode: hjkl navigate. Text mode: typing edits, arrows navigate blocks. ROADMAP Horizon 5.
design:
## Architecture: Vim-Inspired Modal Editing with Shared Primitives

### Model
- Global `mode: 'node' | 'text'` in Zustand store
- Node mode: hjkl navigates between nodes, letters are commands
- Text mode: all chars insert, arrows move within text, Esc exits

### Prior Art
- **Vim/Neovim**: global State variable for mode, separate input handling per mode. Normal mode: keys → command lookup. Insert mode: keys → text insertion.
- **SlateJS**: NodeSelection vs TextSelection — conceptual distinction between selecting whole block vs cursor in text
- **ProseMirror**: NodeSelection (block selected) vs TextSelection (cursor in text) — different behaviors for same keys depending on selection type

### Key Decisions
1. **Explicit mode flag** (not implicit from selection type) — clearer for TUI, prevents ambiguity
2. **Enter or `i` to enter text mode** on current node, **Esc to exit** and save
3. **Separate key maps** per mode — Node mode: command switch. Text mode: character insertion + few special keys (Esc, arrows, Backspace)
4. **Mode indicator** in status line: "[EDITING]" or similar
5. **Share selection primitives** with unified anchor/focus model (see km-tui.selection-abstraction)
6. **Text cursor** lives in `selection.offset` when in text mode; `null` in node mode

### Implementation
1. Add `mode: 'node' | 'text'` + `editingNodeId: string | null` to store
2. Key handler: check mode first, dispatch to appropriate handler
3. Node mode handler: existing command switch (hjkl, etc.)
4. Text mode handler: maintain cursor position in text string, handle char insertion/deletion, arrow movement within text
5. Mode transitions: `enterTextMode(nodeId)` sets mode='text', initializes text cursor. `exitTextMode()` saves content, sets mode='node'
6. React rendering: conditionally show text input UI for editingNodeId
7. Ensure `await delay(0)` or similar when entering text mode so UI can render the editing state
notes:
2026-02-17: EditContext (km-tui.edit-context) answers the 'is there an active text editor?' question. Text mode = active EditContext. Node mode = no active EditContext. Implement after edit-migrate lands.
Implemented text mode as derived state (not separate store field). getEditMode(ui) derives mode from inlineEditBlock + dialog flags. Added EditMode type, getEditMode(), enterTextMode(), exitTextMode(), currentMode() helpers. [EDIT] indicator in bottom bar. 10 tests pass.
Implemented inline-edit-barrier keybinding layer between text layer and detail-pane layer. Adds wildcard catch-all (noop) when isInlineEditing, preventing all node-mode commands (navigation, edit, task, fold, view, quit) from firing during text editing. Undo/redo/yank explicitly bound above the wildcard so they still work. 31 new tests in keybindings.test.ts covering: blocked node-mode keys (Tab, m, q, v, hjkl via noop wildcard), preserved text-editing keys (Escape, Enter, Backspace, arrows, Ctrl combos), undo/redo during editing, and blocked Ctrl combos (Ctrl+d page_down, Ctrl+j sibling_board, Ctrl+i detail_pane, Meta+arrows shift).
